647934811BC242CE979BD7507173E4A9.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

9672B08BC2A045E18CAAADDC6DB99D5C.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

9698D5BD021F461584CCB6B865A8B6D4.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

0682FD0920E845F0B90A6B01F02D763F.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

662D4A8B67FC48CEB7738A0E9F399402.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

FF65EA508B0C478E9612B7FA2B446A68.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

946C82DDE5A84D2A8EA3E8232B8B7C45.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

E6F055D0F82C4A06A2F41E2EB12078D5.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:

C0CAA1CF3C4641B6B6E5A6A5B05D2571.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations

4D052B0CA10D4C1CB8513525FD97AC84.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

5D8D89A995D2474EB29C8A430C867616.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

FDEC82E36AE3436F9B8540BE3BB9AF09.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

11928D17E7994066A30AA32BDA7FA3B7.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

4ED377335AE744ECA04C8DCB58876525.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

B551646B01944BF28A5168AF5873984E.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

C48C676706B849478C53965FF5960D15.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

2EC2AA6496394B5C846B5374ED83C750.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

DA6E1FA6367B4148ADD3551E50D8B531.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions

9015867790C44E0489A954689A2D5F94.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

009E402C5B244EBBB26302C7E9F312E9.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

5B3E0E1BC87847A58B6CC533444944D1.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

8AA0BBA581224ACE83433C6BD6C8F253.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

4CC210563C294E28A1D5BC454C3B7ED0.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

3FF241F12D314136BC853CDE62AA1E1C.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane

D6B3516C97674FCB8BCBA64B23E1E360.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

9640FE86F3764C5487AFA54956E7F3D9.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

798CDF073BCC4CFEA5D7567214A02B4E.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

125A576CA5284427948907AD92F9B771.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

2E820BA87E7643FBABCECA5376401D13.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

0B5DBEC9040044F093A7D716A0B9CC56.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

E1FCD65EA4F94BA0B56859FB8466FD0A.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

DD4301081AD343879CB36B0C0B916184.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

6B903F95D9F64C669B5269E756648866.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

E5C6A082F8C34EF1B12F8195B9CCFF8A.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

B89A869628DB48EFA3DACA0A3ECAC180.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

ECB01A29FB194F418A82BCC4EB466E5B.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

297B5478ADD0417EB904E7F70BE3B43C.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

A350FCFE353D46FEBBF395D64707FB01.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model

6BD391EC609A4327BD41AE3F9CFC0932.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

FBD105E77E6344E6BFCFE32ED5826475.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

0FD43B85BFFA4B68B2ED0028082F5BCB.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

AEFA722C4A9C4FA69484F9C74B325F21.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

052BD7196B254DA6B9A87D270388EB1A.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

127742AD0D704C9B8B679AD3CFB7C008.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

EBF263A5B8B44881AF09F19D5AD46284.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems

2C965097466E4BEE8681524E84F4299C.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

7E89D69FDE35402FAC5A1382D9C3887F.description: Build new functions from existing functions

666ABB77F28D4E3DB5A743A733D0228C.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

2B3F60C66BF24E50A8D6D448B6DD44DF.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

6E37563729434D789516A856CE8087A6.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

A4C3D7761BA44E53A76DBA37BD3F4896.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

CC4989281B554EFFB2D9E226B88EFF07.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

606A1FE3086D406D8F44DBC4125836F1.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

3F7ADDD0F6FD400EA945371FAA639B2C.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

017D06BE493F4CE4A2BC54A271D4B343.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

BAE32450E1B44A20BB5E35F7862E5C90.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

182CA7FB722A4BA9BB1F08BC40E30EE7.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

962A0499C69242C7BE1FC46D9A650441.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

0F954FE19F09487182DB4821D56FF969.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

C37930D231A14433AB8B2B806DD117F9.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

2AAC63B8C0264EFCB416773C7A63D10C.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

37B3E89B246B4A1F96BD49CE0D131079.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

FDD281B23B3E4B3D8B677E1980E5DCE9.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

BEEADE70DD044548ACB08B4D64FA107F.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

5367BB13F5774007B1A8B34654660B96.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

573E0B03F07C44CE86628955663FF534.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

CDCB911F07E5455BB207E344F4BC205B.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

87C2D01D6F7A4C0CADF9F7C1B23967CD.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

41D3B50BD13F44F7B6591BF1430B30AB.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

A54BEE989B834DDEAA40DF8655F0FBD4.description: Given a system of two equations in two variables, show and explain why the sum of equivalent forms of the equations produces the same solution as the original system.

ACAEEF90E9774E46B9CD41A2CD339F52.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

DB0D0426EF7041F58B735CECAEA358B5.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

A2FFE54D02F44B63869314C8921F2041.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

CF6AD9C2EFA54F4C832904761B982809.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

7910210CFA4248478D4A587C9ABC2836.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

DA8B2891A8354B16905676674C004356.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

41339BCE1D2045A193F684D3B2D8A454.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

AE19C7588F2C402D8B62EB16F629858A.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

699D1134A464423A8A0A048AEB5D9FC0.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

F5B02AAFF2F94AA6AC4AF5D3D17AD9FA.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

194E851C801A4728B54444EC8547B768.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

5F5454CF191347FAAF131875CA2F0E63.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

8BF3A77800514B64890B82ACF9D10539.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

5D649DBF2D0244B8BA6CF889F4D00919.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials

637A0BA667944F0887CB8DEB932DBE03.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

0BDCF45B3CDB442BBD7FD8E0BC53537B.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

1563480D58EC4D6480B07FF85F8C0326.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

6F223D7BBE90437CBB9166E8A5DAA912.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

E389C90A55EC4009979F55D608EFBA61.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

B36BD21DDC75495EBA2B20D83E1AA8E1.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

EF61B8AC05764E4C8AEA01B63D3509EC.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

7F24D5C8A93D4AD6965E621D44C4B3BC.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

FFF1EDBB12CC4CE2ACD776497515B039.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

674DB517743B437F9FCD09387A20AA35.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

44029094CA0544C995EBB69CEB5ED2E2.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

BD8D6D44F5854260886803B9B8A6B7F7.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

076EE57C92B7435E837D07CF6D5B3B0E.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

EAADD586F0C745E1BFAB0D32DDA947C1.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

22E680443EBB42EAAFAC26D2876B367C.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems

053975EAE3304E0E8A494262A572F65C.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

EBDD9102E4704138868C36AACF6B9011.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers

document.title: Mississippi College and Career Readiness Standards for Mathematics

7EA7EC98DBC345C3B436A012BB4AEC3F.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

46428F0D35604DCD9337D81DB9EC46A0.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

78D417041D474600912CB53950F3DCF2.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

126516D626994A4BAFF849373471D02D.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles

A03DEED3864D482E82F5236F7BAAD297.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

0511CB0DB0D14D8CBB5C5947306F0084.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

6BAFB73A5226481B8CA948204B94A3C1.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

2676EDC3D7054F118901BAA06F372147.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

63C87CB066564D06B66025FC0DA1F6A7.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

DB0AECD5E8F24B969DA8B98E68A01CAD.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles

77AE4BAC0BB942E081B29E53E5C03F2C.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

3FC18B6FBF1C4F4F958BBCA9A3C441A9.description:
Use the four operations to solve word problems involving
  • distances
  • intervals of time
  • liquid volumes
  • masses of objects
  • money
including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

D5E5A049E6E644838FF08F2EBE3F6461.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

988B560A1A6A4A06BFF58CE40BBCD21D.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit

137239155872493EA8E19B353E9464B5.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

30DD86E9C32449359AD9145C4200EEBC.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

1282F6DF39774D568086B1DCD8D05991.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

D72F9B17B79C4E7196DE969B44348E7B.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

05604B54D9A9433BADC58F7E24D67128.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions

5A65451714834C62875664D64D1D2771.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

DB18DEADF54F406980908C6297A331AD.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

F50C7C96D4D4407589DC5714D2EA0E37.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

3645BC92DC964100B5C1DF29F4739AA1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

3C71A431EC6C4D8983895FD5BF868FDC.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

753ECD42F7924369990EFD149A4D5F43.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

1991843BA0B142E2A1FE2524F3B231CA.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

377E8AC12A954C00B71CD3EF3A7E32F0.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

9B62136270DB4746BCE86E5B2EDB2536.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

891049CB024D414AAFFC0344265839FF.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers

DE037794BDFB4476B6DBA31ECBF6226A.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

E1A6D30F01AA47CDBC40B716A2E190AB.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

A9BE144C9C3946FFB96636320C7D5204.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering

E56360B3E1F14380ABA4EEE1A4E9D25E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

D5B79D960D384ADD9BD8DF76124690A5.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

60626815402C46D1B2EE830D08B4ECFD.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

AB64F9375EAD40629DA3329B2916485C.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers

E15F0E546E9B49DC9BBF3FED0A31D63D.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

3B0A55DF1A0E442AB32A0D30744D9558.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

6A1C181E610945F1AC59001D794F633A.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

86D6DBE1DE1C4CF8820DDDFD1A397107.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic

4309093721534D96990C885108EAC2F5.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

E4887D2E360A4BBDA0DDED8D1DA24D89.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

DD67C505CF0E4764A5457FC86B613E3C.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

C9EC9EBB5D0547938CB08C64325E994C.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples

B09548FDFB9740E4B7854340709FCCE9.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

9C9A8350786C47B58C9823C85E2E5A49.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

959D23465B6C408681BF2D894146754F.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

BA1679706BA04688BCF76B67D727BA50.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. CD2F0BF40AE14A40B6E7B349FD7CB423.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

473B10059AF944EA9AF8A0FE8F967018.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

9BC991CB5B054531B93EA03A112016AD.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten."

F5FDE2FEAF8E4DE98876056CEA3DB622.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

8BE8612F5B0A404F8696B7495D64119F.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

FA546E503A8B48C99BA8B2A3705A61F2.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.

0D958C1D3FA849C9852923C3C130B542.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations

Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

76377624CBDA4279A741BA0C8383315E.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.

2BD816B2D534409DBD6F93D1786761AB.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.

12EA1857DAFB4F0DA1B6A332F8FD2952.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction

58E503D1912A4DA387F97D5063846617.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

965E44845AB04215A3AB249507BF29B7.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

8ED8062C9E3A466B9B44E6B4CBEF4805.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction

C14260A37E0B423BBCC4717981EE3781.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

351C4A2FF461497FB28395F3F23BAE3F.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes

C925D0CD059449F3A0FAAB14124E70DA.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres)

9C3A7DFE2711447BA79162C73576077E.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

747A733B1C75423BBF92D15646D9ACEF.description: Count to tell the number of objects

D7708D6066E6437CB917E7244C8AE8C0.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

83E5F22AFC324F10BA8F2FF4FA27D259.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). 329ECE1E4B1446D3A4D0CA585C1CCC21.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

E2194733C39E49588E5EDCF1EF37D827.description: With teacher guidance, investigate possible solutions to prevent or repair soil erosion.

A10225102D044B88BEDC88B0F9634242.description: Use informational text, other media, and first-hand observations to investigate and communicate the process and consequences of soil erosion.

824FEFFEEBA64A4AA857F879456C2B74.description: Use informational text and other media to summarize and communicate how Earth materials are used (e.g., soil and water to grow plants; rocks to make roads, walls or building; or sand to make glass).

BE0B95449F6F43B991756A469DBAA482.description: Conduct an investigation to identify and classify everyday objects that are resources from the Earth (e.g., drinking water, granite countertops, clay dishes, wood furniture, or gas grill). Classify these objects as renewable and nonrenewable resources.

94C693D3DA8948C48F2EE0F9B1D84BF6.description: Use informational text, other media, and first-hand observations to investigate, analyze and compare the properties of Earth materials (including rocks, soils, sand, and water).

1C94F4FCB44049AEA356EB3480B93BB5.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how humans use Earth's resources.

29B5D14742FC4481A264F3009003FE28.description: Create a model that will demonstrate the observable pattern of motion of the Sun or Moon. Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the model.

8595D62385F54586919A9C9B27F510AD.description: Use informational text and other media to observe, describe and predict the visual patterns of motion of the Sun (sunrise, sunset) and Moon (phases).

82E35E0C74F541E583B6EF2208776757.description: With teacher support, gain an understanding that scientists are humans who use observations and experiments to learn about space. Obtain information from informational text or other media about scientists who have made important discoveries about objects in space (e.g., Galileo Galilei, Johannes Kepler, George Ellery Hale, Jill Tarter) or the development of technologies (e.g., various telescopes and detection devices, computer modeling, and space exploration).

7569ADBCFA9C4AD1998AA9B656E82404.description: Observe and compare the details in images of the moon and planets using the perspective of the naked eye, telescopes, and data from space exploration.

926F7152F169493E8D0DDFCC6D29929A.description: With teacher guidance, observe, describe, and predict the seasonal patterns of sunrise and sunset. Collect, represent, and interpret data from internet sources to communicate findings.

81A4A77DF27043CCA390343855085F23.description: Recognize that there are many stars that can be observed in the night sky and the Sun is the Earth's closest star.

AA46075E552F484CAC757E07158FF712.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the appearance, movements, and patterns of the sun, moon, and stars.

3C8A8FDFBFF443BBBD8432AA9EBE5FFD.description: Develop a plan to change the force (push or pull) of friction to solve a human problem (e.g., improve the ride on a playground slide or make a toy car or truck go faster). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the plan.

C02D4E6C5DF247BE8CF875D2C3FFCBCC.description: Generate and answer questions about the relationship between (1) friction and the motion of objects and (2) friction and the production of heat.

98E8854AC80442168F532AC66DD40D10.description: Conduct a structured investigation to collect, represent, and analyze data from observations and measurements to demonstrate the effects of pushes and pulls with different strengths and directions. Communicate findings (e.g., models or technology).

BE37C1DF2AF44EA8821602130D85842B.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how the motion of objects is affected by pushes, pulls, and friction on an object.

863C7BED4FBC4EFE838C344B98B3BEF2.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims that some changes to matter caused by heating can be reversed, and some changes cannot be reversed.

60E24133B0754493B844FC38BCD324EE.description: Compare the weight of solid objects and the volume of liquid objects. Analyze and communicate findings.

E80C43CC95B242F8B302937BF325EF29.description: Compare and measure the length of solid objects using technology and mathematical representations. Analyze and communicate findings.

2C21509DEF1A43F18078F86814CE077D.description: Conduct a structured investigation to collect, represent, and analyze categorical data to classify matter as solid, liquid, or gas. Report findings and describe a variety of materials according to observable physical properties (e.g., size, color, texture, opacity, solubility).

77222055F3AA4A27A95555013D10718C.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the properties of matter.

8DC834C2D29147839029B1655C1C4B69.description: Organization of Matter and Chemical Interactions

9B06472D537647658555A6B8314EDE3C.description: Obtain and communicate examples of physical features or behaviors of vertebrates and invertebrates and how these characteristics help them survive in particular environments, (e.g., animals hibernate, migrate, or estivate to stay alive when food is scarce or temperatures are not favorable).

77725A51207A467E9AFB61B572568AB7.description: Examine evidence to communicate information that the internal and external structures of plant (e.g., thorns, leaves, stems, roots, or colored petals) function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.

6DBE086197CF4F9A971341A6E7C2D3DE.description: Examine evidence to communicate information that the internal and external structures of animals (e.g., heart, stomach, bone, lung, brain, skin, ears, appendages) function to support survival, growth, and behavior.

C5E42ADB9F0D4E979B37FEB97EBA311A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of internal and external structures in plants and animals and how they relate to their growth, survival, behavior, and reproduction within an environment.

729FB55565F246249D07231271E499E2.description: Create a solution exemplified by animal adaptations to solve a human problem in a specific environment (e.g., snowshoes are like hare's feet or flippers are like duck's feet). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the solution.

CC227C1CCAAA4200BF83633192634676.description: Evaluate and communicate findings from informational text or other media to describe how plants and animals use adaptations to survive (e.g., ducks use webbed feet to swim in lakes and ponds, cacti have waxy coatings and spines to grow in the desert) in distinct environments (e.g., polar lands, saltwater and freshwater, desert, rainforest, woodlands).

E99CCF1B348A41B0BD46A275E3F789B3.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the ways animals adapt to their environment in order to survive.

B6F09B518B5149EFAF126B0E15AC6EC0.description: Conduct an investigation to find evidence where plants and animals compete or cooperate with other plants and animals for food or space. Present findings (i.e., using technology or models).

330A7CA4870449F09B3876100A55451C.description: Evaluate and communicate findings from informational text or other media to describe and to compare how animals interact with other animals and plants in the environment (i.e., predator-prey relationships, herbivore, carnivore, omnivore).

A4C91DF439EB41CF81D0035F25422B99.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interdependence of living things.

9BC3A97F22DB4F8E932432FAEBA8CDF4.description: Construct scientific arguments to explain how animals can make major changes (e.g., beaver dams obstruct streams, or large deer populations destroying crops) and minor changes to their environments (e.g., ant hills, crawfish burrows, mole tunnels). Communicate findings.

2809248F0E6A453AA17A90E8DE933A5E.description: Evaluate and communicate findings from informational text or other media to describe how animals change and respond to rapid or slow changes in their environment (fire, pollution, changes in tide, availability of food/water).

0A3179AA1C524EBE83A0CDE631DDF30C.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interdependence of living things and the environment in which they live.

00056979011844CAB192B79DDBF9C152.description: Construct explanations using first-hand observations or other media to describe the life cycle of an amphibian (birth, growth/development, reproduction, and death). Communicate findings.

F925D8701F494DA6A26A2B960776B0CB.description: Use observations through informational texts and other media to observe the different stages of the life cycle of trees (i.e., pines, oaks) to construct explanations and compare how trees change and grow over time.

B2FB9F3675B045A5BAC8A9C690A396C3.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how living things change in form as they go through the general stages of a life cycle.

895726971893457DAA60DE165F19A9A0.description: Construct a scientific argument for classifying vertebrates that have unusual characteristics, such as bats, penguins, snakes, salamanders, dolphins, and duck-billed platypuses (i.e., bats have wings yet they are mammals).

0B0B4F8C2EBF4287A1B724908D04FD29.description: Compare and contrast physical characteristics that distinguish classes of vertebrates (i.e., reptiles compared to amphibians).

600E9748D8894A6FB6257B132294E5AF.description: Classify vertebrates (mammals, fish, birds, amphibians, and reptiles) based on their physical characteristics.

350E222B4ABB4D7C89273F8C7866E534.description: Compare and sort groups of animals with backbones (vertebrates) from groups of animals without backbones (invertebrates).

BABA24DFC34A4E53833184D6FEA10427.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the classification of animals based on physical characteristics.

386DBE90FA6A40059B1B0651A83B30A6.description: With teacher guidance, generate and answer questions to develop a simple model, which describes observable patterns of sunlight on the Earth's surface (day and night).

7D649DE1F6F440819F99FD62C0B22C89.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that the Sun provides the Earth with heat and light.

F301B185DC204E9C8B25BE62DD5BB472.description: Construct an explanation of the pattern of the Earth's seasonal changes in the environment using evidence from observations.

22E2099262AC49D1A00D533BB34763A1.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the pattern of seasonal changes on the Earth.

0C99D24F67834117B0EEB6822558212D.description: Explain why things may not work the same if some of the parts are missing.

AC94E42D7E664369A734548EAC61758B.description: Analyze a large composite structure to describe its smaller components using drawing and writing.

EC007FCE41D948E19EA19828F0049CCB.description: Use basic shapes and spatial reasoning to model large objects in the environment using a set of small objects (e.g., blocks, construction sets).

8B5AB7C3D52A4BE08CD16A456B69CF49.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how solid objects can be constructed from a smaller set.

FDE66E6CE9B243DCB0E6B4FA342677AE.description: Describe and compare the properties of different materials (e.g., wood, plastic, metal, cloth, paper) and classify these materials by their observable characteristics (visual, aural, or natural textural) and by their physical properties (weight, volume, solid or liquid, and sink or float).

5BC24687628F472C9910543923C6F665.description: Generate questions and investigate the differences between liquids and solids and develop awareness that a liquid can become a solid and vice versa.

0227FA7778C54AF6A078361B806FF28D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the solid and liquid states of matter.

5E0AC184C3E34D8D96036E02B0F6EF75.description: Organization of Matter and Chemical Interactions

513BC36A3E074D7CBA957BD6DA1D5847.description: Observe and report how some present-day animals resemble extinct animals (i.e., elephants resemble wooly mammoths).

D5DA55896CAB4CE5A4A6F5CBC67323D8.description: Obtain information from informational text or other media to document and report examples of different plants or animals that are extinct.

AC37976FED644007844ED66A834ECD15.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that some groups of plants and animals are no longer living (extinct) because they were unable to meet their needs for survival.

7299C123EFF84EB185AA075F4B67079E.description: Create a model habitat which demonstrates interdependence of plants and animals using an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the habitat.

6A1A6477E58443EDA06F948E224FE4EE.description: Observe and communicate that animals get food from plants or other animals. Plants make their own food and need light to live and grow.

E678D554D3F445C0A910CC5FFB2BC2E0.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interdependence of living things and the environment in which they live.

5630B8BF20F64034B4742C600A4B18E6.description: Construct explanations using observations to describe and report what animals need to live and grow (food, water, shelter, and space).

A4D311B4A7BB4E6FB35D401B7CB61C83.description: With teacher guidance, conduct a structured investigation to determine what plants need to live and grow (water, light, and a place to grow). Measure growth by directly comparing plants with other objects.

0EE4CFC8AD224C7EBF8BA8F634A04836.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of what animals and plants need to live and grow.

B6A2F89E2CC6427DA064936534E2792D.description: Use observations to explain that young plants and animals are like but not exactly like their parents (i.e., puppies look similar, but not exactly like their parents).

59EEBD2AB8E94DB88BE45DAB525AB9EF.description: With teacher guidance, conduct a structured investigation to observe and measure (comparison of lengths) the changes in various individuals of a single plant species from seed germination to adult plant. Record observations using drawing or writing.

F667853892994C7893E41634E180221B.description: Construct explanations using observations to describe and model the life cycle (birth, growth, adulthood, death) of a familiar mammal (e.g., dog, squirrel, rabbit, deer).

D5C3E64ACCD84A038AC8EA45F2752D66.description: Use informational text or other media to make observations about plants as they change during the life cycle (e.g., germination, growth, reproduction, and death) and use models (e.g., drawing, writing, dramatization, or technology) to communicate findings.

2976148AF3534204885A8F636BDA751A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how living things change in form as they go through the general stages of a life cycle.

F3F5563FCE8648BF9039BC5BA778C453.description: Identify and describe examples of how animals use their sensory body parts (eyes to detect light and movement, ears to detect sound, skin to detect temperature and touch, tongue to taste, and nose to detect smell).

2E2A0218165F4A258DF37E05ADAC8286.description: Develop and use models to exemplify how animals use their body parts to (a) obtain food and other resources, (b) protect themselves, and (c) move from place to place.

3FC5A1154CB14F4F8BF97021EABFFF34.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how animals (including humans) use their physical features and their senses to learn about their environment.

A36083377C0C42DCA6A09C6E364CC275.description: With teacher support, gain an understanding that scientists are humans who use observations to learn about the natural world. Obtain information from informational text or other media about scientists who have made important observations about living things (e.g. Carl Linnaeus, John James Audubon, Jane Goodall).

308EB5A638C7423C80F63962530A7581.description: With teacher guidance, conduct an investigation of living organisms and nonliving objects in various real-world environments to define characteristics of living organisms that distinguish them from nonliving things (e.g., playground, garden, school grounds).

CE92FE9E9CAB4F71905AF7339568EED8.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of living and nonliving things.

279F8004936A4320B880C7388DD76DD1.description: Analyze and interpret data from the surface features of the Sun (e.g., photosphere, corona, sunspots, prominences, and solar flares) to predict how these features may affect Earth.

1A5ED15B21664F4FB5C85DA92DD781D1.description: Design models representing motions within the Sun-Earth-Moon system to explain phenomena observed from the Earth's surface (positions of celestial bodies, day and year, moon phases, solar and lunar eclipses, and tides).

7120BE52032D4324804062B578C2FB1F.description: Construct explanations for how gravity affects the motion of objects in the solar system and tides on Earth.

6D6E805CCAF54B81ACAEBDA7E2EB27DD.description: Obtain and evaluate information to model and compare the characteristics and movements of objects in the solar system (including planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and meteors).

DE58939C6FB24897B9C07A03032CAB84.description: Evaluate modern techniques used to explore our solar system's position in the universe.

6D248ACFB23A46AAABA3908DF82DE8EF.description: Use graphical displays or models to explain the hierarchical structure (stars, galaxies, galactic clusters) of the universe.

6C557DFC3EB34F44930AE9995C2F103B.description: Obtain, evaluate, and summarize past and present theories and evidence to explain the formation and composition of the universe.

475F994A57B2476C88C7A01AF3D3536D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of Earth's place in the universe and the interactions of the solar system (sun, planets, their moons, comets, and asteroids) using evidence from multiple scientific resources to explain how these objects are held in orbit around the Sun because of its gravitational pull.

A5E60C8DC89B435AB9D991135ED41DEB.description: Determine the relationships between the concepts of potential, kinetic, and thermal energy.

3CA907C0B4C34320809CCB64DA107FE4.description: Investigate forces (gravity, friction, drag, lift, thrust) acting on objects (e.g., airplane, bicycle helmets). Use data to explain the differences between the forces in various environments.

1DD57BA453F44FBBB92DB360A91437B6.description: Conduct investigations to predict and explain the motion of an object according to its position, direction, speed, and acceleration.

2110C4B8CDCD4785AE09E04F573D176C.description: Compare and contrast magnetic, electric, frictional, and gravitational forces.

1149F554FEE745878B6A28241D08F2CD.description: Investigate and communicate ways to manipulate applied/frictional forces to improve movement of objects on various surfaces (e.g., athletic shoes, wheels on cars).

86E93EF3DBFF47B5B482C62B16FC689C.description: Use mathematical computation and diagrams to calculate the sum of forces acting on various objects.

13A6BE7B778A4913A1C4766101276413.description: Use an engineering design process to create or improve safety devices (e.g., seat belts, car seats, helmets) by applying Newton's Laws of motion. Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the safety device.

1EBECDB96CF643BC901E41F4A137762D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of Newton's laws of motion using real world models and examples.

FA40F334D3054B328632CEF63BB82222.description: Engage in scientific arguments to support claims that bacteria (Archaebacteria and Eubacteria) and viruses can be both helpful and harmful to other organisms and the environment.

DF63A3C93E794D22B2A6972E350AC3EB.description: Conduct investigations using a microscope or multimedia source to compare the characteristics of protists (euglena, paramecium, amoeba) and the methods they use to obtain energy and move through their environment (e.g., pond water).

9FD632E493754B98AE7FB5BA9548CBEC.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations to describe how fungi obtain energy and respond to stimuli (e.g., bread mold, rotting plant material).

34D8FDE45F97428BA8C017A9291C78C8.description: Use classification methods to explore the diversity of organisms in kingdoms (animals, plants, fungi, protists, bacteria). Support claims that organisms have shared structural and behavioral characteristics.

71C65F4B5F1742E492201D0A4C140C87.description: Compare and contrast modern classification techniques (e.g., analyzing genetic material) to the historical practices used by scientists such as Aristotle and Carolus Linnaeus.

7109AAF96EC04C2FA7AF8096622E2A90.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of classification tools and models such as dichotomous keys to classify representative organisms based on the characteristics of the kingdoms: Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, Protists, Fungi, Plants, and Animals.

29FCF0E1F06D4421BFDD580F11E94D1E.description: Develop and use food chains, webs, and pyramids to analyze how energy is transferred through an ecosystem from producers (autotrophs) to consumers (heterotrophs, including humans) to decomposers.

9172851FC69D45518B50E3F1FBB667EB.description: Investigate organism interactions in a competitive or mutually beneficial relationship (predation, competition, cooperation, or symbiotic relationships).

9EF81703561B4630A7703DC5739138D3.description: Analyze cause and effect relationships to explore how changes in the physical environment (limiting factors, natural disasters) can lead to population changes within an ecosystem.

67D96E2D506E4EB28253EC4FC6D48770.description: Develop and use models to describe the levels of organization within ecosystems (species, populations, communities, ecosystems, and biomes).

26E08C812182443A8CC59D1FB25E400A.description: Use scientific reasoning to explain differences between biotic and abiotic factors that demonstrate what living organisms need to survive.

D4E93947D631468C8F257E1C3779BE81.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the relationships among survival, environmental changes, and diversity as they relate to the interactions of organisms, populations, and the environment.

839057FEFC144CC19B2A5C42081387DF.description: Develop and use models to show relationships among the increasing complexity of multicellular organisms (cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, organisms) and how they serve the needs of the organism.

500E7B2C17164C89AE8A9C3B49B43AE8.description: Provide evidence that organisms are unicellular or multicellular.

FB91187CB77149CB8A7F475A340FEEF5.description: Compare and contrast different cells in order to classify them as a protist, fungus, plant, or animal.

55FFE582333D4D00A32EE05BF932BD1E.description: Develop and use models to explain how specific cellular components (cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, chloroplast, vacuole, and mitochondria) function together to support the life of prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms to include plants, animals, fungi, protists, and bacteria (not to include biochemical function of cells or cell part).

C8EAFD7A70324A88BCA5932DCCAE70E0.description: Obtain and communicate evidence to support the cell theory.

546B2D82146E4B0DB00877157AB69E3D.description: Use argument supported by evidence in order to distinguish between living and non-living things, including viruses and bacteria.

904605A757F846CA8A882F21026D907E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that living things range from simple to complex organisms, are organized hierarchically, and function as whole living systems.
