C7D80D7ADF284795AF96008800320A16.description: Investigate how variations of sunlight intensity experienced by each hemisphere (to include the equator and poles) create the four seasons.

A0BEE5BFAADD4BC19B424E92B6123924.description: Construct models and diagrams to illustrate how the tilt of Earth's axis results in differences in intensity of sunlight on the Earth's hemispheres throughout the course of one full revolution around the Sun.

764D9F07821F4C0781DB92AF2753F52E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that the seasons are the direct result of the Earth's tilt and the intensity of sunlight on the Earth's hemispheres.

3F56444F142041CABD72D840B988E455.description: Engage in scientific argument based on current evidence to determine whether climate change happens naturally or is being accelerated through the influence of man.

E2111C48F5244CECA2974A3BE274ECBF.description: Interpret data about the relationship between the release of carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels into the atmosphere and the presence of greenhouse gases.

130BFBCA0A6440358671F1DBBF12939E.description: Read and evaluate scientific or technical information assessing the evidence and bias of each source to explain the causes and effects of climate change.

06058152B24B49D69E543A2324C6660E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between natural phenomena, human activity, and global climate change.

8E8345D320B44C338B203C977B9F38E4.description: Interpret topographic maps to predict how local and regional geography affect weather patterns and make them difficult to predict.

14EBA48FC98C4466A28D2DBFB42ED65D.description: Research and use models to explain what type of weather (thunderstorms, hurricanes, and tornadoes) results from the movement and interactions of air masses, high and low pressure systems, and frontal boundaries.

A7CF6E4A49BB422DA5AB4DFA8149E6C7.description: Analyze models to explain the cause and effect relationship between solar energy and convection and the resulting weather patterns and climate conditions.

A247729FA2194C9496E32B22B7224834.description: Construct an explanation for how climate is determined in an area using global and surface features (e.g. latitude, elevation, shape of the land, distance from water, global winds and ocean currents).

9AA9778F4A224DC3A059BBC46AA6A7DF.description: Interpret atmospheric data from satellites, radar, and weather maps to predict weather patterns and conditions.

054AEE99672F4EDAB8D1F79C33233BBF.description: Analyze evidence to explain the weather conditions that result from the relationship between the movement of water and air masses.

A78FFE7595E040B0A1033FDDFBAC45DF.description: Analyze and interpret weather patterns from various regions to differentiate between weather and climate.

B178684F6D454F08AF9175398D8A488D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how complex changes in the movement and patterns of air and water molecules caused by the sun, winds, landforms, ocean temperatures, and currents in the atmosphere are major determinants of local and global weather patterns.

6F2762E98D6041109E53183EABAA212C.description: Compare and contrast balanced and unbalanced chemical equations to demonstrate the number of atoms does not change in the reaction.

F53A8D9D01E44207B924ABEC6870D0B3.description: Analyze data from investigations to explain why the total mass of the product in an open system appears to be less than the mass of reactants.

949B5FF0BF7A48DBA008495445C7DA90.description: Conduct simple scientific investigations to show that total mass is not altered during a chemical reaction in a closed system. Compare results of investigations to Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier's discovery of the law of conservation of mass.

6877C32BE9D54FF786A45DAFCDBD3816.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the law of conservation of mass.

2372FBB6B7BF4337918284C8921C28F3.description: Build a model to explain that chemical reactions can store (formation of bonds) or release energy (breaking of bonds).

7DD82E42B52849C5A4D87CE75EBDCE00.description: Collect, organize, and interpret data using various tools (e.g., litmus paper, pH paper, cabbage juice) regarding neutralization of acids and bases using common substances.

C18447CE76E24254925227DF9E272231.description: Design and conduct scientific investigations to support evidence that chemical reactions (e.g., cooking, combustion, rusting, decomposition, photosynthesis, and cellular respiration) have occurred.

10F267FB2B46432CB8F8815FBED04CDF.description: Analyze evidence from scientific investigations to predict likely outcomes of chemical reactions.

93C66D459A944415B0BFA02A74C1DD8D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of chemical formulas and common chemical substances to predict the types of reactions and possible outcomes of the reactions.

C19836D065DB4AFDB08986B27EBE2DB1.description: Using the periodic table, make predictions to explain how bonds (ionic and covalent) form between groups of elements (e.g., oxygen gas, ozone, water, table salt, and methane).

D6B675B94D7E4EFA8CCA99FC8CF2754B.description: Describe concepts used to construct chemical formulas (e.g. CH4, H20) to determine the number of atoms in a chemical formula.

57F7A6A74A8A4B83B632ED256C8D431D.description: Predict the properties and interactions of elements using the periodic table (metals, non-metals, reactivity, and conductors).

AA3084D9B7C8425CBD86E34701DCCE03.description: Collect, organize, and interpret data from investigations to identify and analyze the relationships between the physical and chemical properties of elements, atoms, molecules, compounds, solutions, and mixtures.

80E8475B14004C5783933312C0D0E5C2.description: Use informational text to sequence the major discoveries leading to the current atomic model.

84D111A869234E4DA1A2C7E5A868DA7D.description: Develop and use models that explain the structure of an atom.

10CC5F0503EE4A6887E68C9AF6288FC6.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the proper use of the periodic table to predict and identify elemental properties and how elements interact.

ED09C4081A2B4DC59EE357DB3CD522DB.description: Ask questions to explain how density of matter (observable in various objects) is affected by a change in heat and/or pressure.

D35E70BE1BDF492C8CCBC8C18CCA91FB.description: Use evidence from multiple scientific investigations to communicate the relationships between pressure, volume, density, and temperature of a gas.

9BE3F0D5D4AD458B8F74D61BCA3514A9.description: Make predictions about the effect of temperature and pressure on the relative motion of atoms and molecules (speed, expansion, and condensation) relative to recent breakthroughs in polymer and materials science (e.g. self-healing protective films, silicone computer processors, pervious/porous concrete).

3E07698B523F4632BCAFAC9A56A7CA64.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding about the effects of temperature and pressure on physical state, molecular motion, and molecular interactions.

D6A4040981D447EF819BFA00291645B4.description: Compare and contrast chemical and physical properties (e.g., combustion, oxidation, pH, solubility, reaction with water).

EEA0A7059F784C498A9A3D59D24C76B7.description: Analyze and interpret qualitative data to describe substances using chemical properties (the ability to burn or rust).

20FFA2E229B340DAB77EC1EE886E2C83.description: Collect and evaluate qualitative data to describe substances using physical properties (state, boiling/melting point, density, heat/electrical conductivity, color, and magnetic properties).

1CBCDA2B88C243B6BE95A1DDB5A0F2E0.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of matter.

3A42FCF1337641AE87AB784B546892F2.description: Organization of Matter and Chemical Interactions

A7EDB61E25E542E7A348EEF07E42BAB0.description: Design solutions for sustaining the health of ecosystems to maintain biodiversity and the resources needed by humans for survival (e.g., water purification, nutrient recycling, prevention of soil erosion, and prevention or management of invasive species).

FB8AD39C5ADF4117A06EE0E07A887110.description: Explain how disruptions in cycles (e.g., water, oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen) affect biodiversity and ecosystem services (e.g., water, food, and medications) which are needed to sustain human life on Earth.

02EE22A004EC4984B483D5495BD0A144.description: Use models to describe how food molecules (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins) are processed through chemical reactions using oxygen (aerobic) to form new molecules.

8FC5E077DB4645158D757ADDB298F7FE.description: Analyze and interpret data to explain how the processes of photosynthesis, and cellular respiration (aerobic and anaerobic) work together to meet the needs of plants and animals.

AFA681E4AA7D43818097E48F6F6AED27.description: Analyze diagrams to provide evidence of the importance of the cycling of water, oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen through ecosystems to organisms.

07AEB61C1C44466FA6D4EC4989737919.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the importance that matter cycles between living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem to sustain life on Earth.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

257674932EF74DBF8547F51B6F7752A9.description: Use technology or informational text to investigate, evaluate, and communicate various forms of clean energy generation.

94508CE3F6C44993B23111C46FEDF803.description: Organize simple data sets to compare energy and pollution output of various traditional, non-renewable resources (e.g. coal, crude oil, wood).

37FB2AB7C5204754A62EE7F38719B100.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the various sources of energy used for human needs along with their effectiveness and possible impacts.

6947441D86FD49CF9ABC76129773744A.description: Obtain and communicate information about severe weather phenomena (e.g., thunderstorms, hurricanes, or tornadoes) to explain steps humans can take to reduce the impact of severe weather events.

BB7070D4EA354B62B54B7476373ACB42.description: Research and explain how systems (i.e., the atmosphere, geosphere, and/or hydrosphere), interact and support life in the biosphere.

821B974CD6084356BB3321144A3C977E.description: Construct scientific arguments from evidence to support claims that human activities, such as conservation efforts or pollution, affect the land, oceans, and atmosphere of Earth.

DDD455DEE2FB4C3D80C3C55354C96242.description: Develop and use models of natural processes to explain the effect of the movement of water on the ocean shore zone, including beaches, barrier islands, estuaries, and inlets (e.g., marshes, bays, lagoons, fjord, or sound).

6B2C829D7E54469F9EBAC23C6550BA8D.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe and predict how natural processes (e.g., weathering, erosion, deposition, earthquakes, tsunamis, hurricanes, or storms) affect Earth's surface.

DDAF8711683144869209AA2F2087908F.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how natural processes and human activities affect the features of Earth's landforms and oceans.

AEFAA1DB674547D6BAE973203B4631D3.description: Design weather instruments utilized to measure weather conditions (e.g., barometer, hygrometer, rain gauge, anemometer, or wind vane). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the weather instrument.

6470D8F0633847028245F899D4B98AAC.description: Construct explanations about regional climate differences using maps and long-term data from various regions.

F09AE2D758874E3FA1A781B8429A4110.description: Analyze and interpret data (e.g., temperature, precipitation, wind speed/direction, relative humidity, or cloud types) to predict changes in weather over time.

A4430B774EAB4D04AF0BFB8D04AB178D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of weather and climate patterns.

3A367BC8D4F840A2AB21CA4231BDDE92.description: Develop and use models to explain how the sun's energy drives the water cycle. (e.g., evaporation, condensation, precipitation, transpiration, runoff, and groundwater).

38FBE19D122443408C05338647F6DDEE.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how the water cycle is propelled by the sun's energy.

04E1E8E5F0B140A7904D890D6D1EA392.description: Obtain and communicate information about scientists who pioneered in the science of sound, (e.g., Alexander Graham Bell, Robert Boyle, Daniel Bernoulli, and Guglielmo Marconi).

D8C9677665EE4DD4BEC0446C2B96CE89.description: In relation to how sound is perceived by humans, analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to report how changes in vibration affect the pitch and volume of sound.

D323293045974B0195D56BEC23D25AA7.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to test how different variables affect the properties of sound (i.e., pitch and volume).

6582BD6E163A4FF1A78EC716B320465F.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the properties of sound as a form of energy.

88AD732FE88145E281DA38A30E7ABC74.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to explain how light behaves when it strikes transparent, translucent, and opaque materials.

E4DE6250E9664C4192060453BC3716CA.description: Develop and use models to communicate how light travels and behaves when it strikes an object, including reflection, refraction, and absorption.

6139AFB93D0E40C893D971C2064F92AE.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain how the visibility of an object is related to light.

9E12FA47C6244029957A6A20959E6C39.description: Construct scientific evidence to support the claim that white light is made up of different colors. Include the work of Sir Isaac Newton to communicate results.

D24FDB9766EB4492A2A89FFB676A150A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the properties of light as forms of energy.

CF6AD44628004F3D849F84B4BEB81B0B.description: Design a device that converts any form of energy from one form to another form (e.g., construct a musical instrument that will convert vibrations to sound by controlling varying pitches, a solar oven that will convert energy from the sun to heat energy, or a simple circuit that can be used to complete a task). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the device.

37FFCE490E184F43AB21858E1CFA6CF6.description: Use informational text and technology resources to communicate technological breakthroughs made by historical figures in electricity (e.g. Alessandro Volta, Michael Faraday, Nicola Tesla, Thomas Edison, incandescent light bulbs, batteries, Light Emitting Diodes).

B489F0C650A94A98843C01AC4CC68683.description: Develop models that demonstrate the path of an electric current in a complete, simple circuit (e.g., lighting a light bulb or making a sound).

9327D987F42949B8BB6B19DA3BC6FFE4.description: Develop models demonstrating how heat and electrical energy can be transformed into other forms of energy (e.g., motion, sound, heat, or light).

62B9DB6991EE4239B3B39CC49659476E.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to classify different materials as either an insulator or conductor of electricity.

0DFFC5AE75F246F1B6957657A528235B.description: Obtain and communicate information to compare how different processes (including burning, friction, and electricity) serve as sources of heat energy.

6019E83541D944929DE7ED28826637B2.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the common sources and uses of heat and electric energy and the materials used to transfer heat and electricity.

4023ED07E70A4FE89DEB8559DDA1A3B3.description: Develop and use models to explain the unique and diverse life cycles of organisms other than humans (e.g., flowering plants, frogs, or butterflies) including commonalities (e.g., birth, growth, reproduction, or death).

539C95DBCBDF454FA1109F099466877B.description: Compare and contrast life cycles of familiar plants and animals.

C52A7B0428964FC392BD89171DEBD063.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of life cycles, including familiar plants and animals (e.g., reptiles, amphibians, or birds).

563490F15EA34F7386BCB243AD23B21D.description: Using informational text, investigate how scientific fields, medical specialties, and research methods help us find new ways to maintain a healthy body and lifestyle (e.g. diet, exercise, vaccines, and mental health).

AD7D0074805E4CE4B3DD9ADF96786D92.description: Research and communicate how noninfectious diseases (e.g. diabetes, heart disease) and infectious diseases (e.g. cold, flu) serve to disrupt the function of the body system.

0D0A35377B324EB1B28D24AD81C2A7C4.description: Construct models of organ systems (e.g. circulatory, digestive, respiratory, muscular, skeletal, nervous) to demonstrate both the unique function of the system and how multiple organs and organ systems work together to accomplish more complex functions.

FA2E4C5185354B8F9E37F1B4383A6380.description: Obtain and communicate data to describe patterns that indicate the nature of relationships between human organ systems, which interact with one another to control digestion, respiration, circulation, excretion, movement, coordination, and protection from infection.

55F83EBB6B9B43C6B6537B04AD8A10AF.description: Use technology or other resources to research and discover general system function (e.g., machines, water cycle) as they relate to human organ systems and identify organs that work together to create organ systems.

01AA3EC882E34F0FAE3D8ADAC3EABB70.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the organization, functions, and interconnections of the major human body systems.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

0E122231FF8642068407158367D18C61.description: Using an engineering design process, develop a system to capture and distribute thermal energy that makes renewable energy more readily available and reduces human impact on the environment (e.g., building solar water heaters, conserving home energy).

33409540682D46F89EA6118DDF7395AF.description: Using scientific data, debate the societal advantages and disadvantages of technological advancements in renewable energy sources.

05CD32DE34E64733ACF3DE2C56FB953D.description: Create and defend a proposal for reducing the environmental effects humans have on Earth (e.g., population increases, consumer demands, chemical pollution, deforestation, and change in average annual temperature).

BEFECC62BB5A468899B8B60C9C5856BA.description: Read and evaluate scientific information about advancements in renewable and nonrenewable resources. Propose and defend ways to decrease national and global dependency on nonrenewable resources.

070F31F6A29A4DA8AFF8D959A62F66F8.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that a decrease in natural resources is directly related to the increase in human population on Earth and must be conserved.

F759930FC21F46A4AD8F865D0287189A.description: Using an engineering design process, create mechanisms to improve community resilience, which safeguard against natural hazards (e.g., building restrictions in flood or tidal zones, regional watershed management, Firewise construction).

7C07FAC58FF84CCEB0AD46A2A57709FC.description: Compare and contrast technologies that predict natural hazards to identify which types of technologies are most effective.

4E01A3665C4D4FD093F1B5DEBEFAE302.description: Research and map various types of natural hazards to determine their impact on society.

AC1EF6563B46434795227B3BC0A0E2EE.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of natural hazards (volcanic eruptions, severe weather, earthquakes) and construct explanations for why some hazards are predictable and others are not.

7C47E99B32A7491D8D6840D5DC2D66A3.description: Explain the interconnected relationship between surface water and groundwater.

FDAF1D335EA44A3DBD9C4D561CFF8EF3.description: Design and conduct investigations to evaluate the chemical and physical processes involved in the formation of soils.

AA0D0EA21698447496229FF5FFB56EA9.description: Use models that demonstrate convergent and divergent plate movements that are responsible for most landforms and the distribution of most rocks and minerals within Earth's crust.

65A4972BB99449D4B092259442FAD94F.description: Research and assess the credibility of scientific ideas to debate and discuss how Earth's constructive and destructive processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.

4D90C9FE564845E1B4F669AFCFE0047F.description: Map land and water patterns from various time periods and use rocks and fossils to report evidence of how Earth's plates have moved great distances, collided, and spread apart.

C2F858489F4E40A495E440A3B7D84A69.description: Explore and debate theories of plate tectonics to form conclusions about past and current movements of rocks at Earth's surface throughout history.

1CEF5AE4D65B4F2088CFE8D1EB69B1C4.description: Investigate and explain how the flow of Earth's internal energy drives the cycling of matter through convection currents between Earth's surface and the deep interior causing plate movements.

8923518C884849C09F54AD483A1CC066.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that physical processes and major geological events (e.g., plate movement, volcanic activity, mountain building, weathering, erosion) are powered by the Sun and the Earth's internal heat and have occurred over millions of years.

6B8BC36EC8954A14A4B5CE623026BFB8.description: Use research and evidence to document how evolution has been shaped both gradually and through mass extinction by Earth's varying geological conditions (e.g., climate change, meteor impacts, and volcanic eruptions).

AEBE439DA97F4D93979EBC0707A95AC9.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims that most fossil evidence is an indication of the diversity of life that was present on Earth and that relationships exist between past and current life forms.

6C60ADB2D16446968F3D89ED3E28446D.description: Create a model of the processes involved in the rock cycle and relate it to the fossil record.

991935DBD82C4388A9D703FBB1A90326.description: Use scientific evidence to create a timeline of Earth's history that depicts relative dates from index fossil records and layers of rock (strata).

1254773BC6564435A2FD9718E2635E91.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of geological evidence to analyze patterns in Earth's major events, processes, and evolution in history.

3207B430AC2B4448892B203B16139A53.description: Compare and contrast the behavior of sound and light waves to determine which types of waves need a medium for transmission.

E6A5E9D09A6046989761A2C819BF8B86.description: Research the historical significance of wave technology to explain how digitized tools have evolved to encode and transmit information (e.g., telegraph, cell phones, and wireless computer networks).

C15E3A5D223545D69F849A3B81ECFD1B.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to explain the relationship between seeing color and the transmission, absorption, or reflection of light waves by various materials.

BB651A9B1A394B3196A7D20F9D82BC4F.description: Conduct scientific investigations that describe the behavior of sound when resonance changes (e.g., waves in a stretched string and design of musical instruments).

B84E08FDF2B24450909A1AA937B5FEDF.description: Use scientific processes to plan and conduct controlled investigations to conclude sound is a wave phenomenon that is characterized by amplitude and frequency.

DBF8623FAEF34A4C8F9D5337D6803F1B.description: Conduct simple investigations about the performance of waves to describe their behavior (e.g., refraction, reflection, transmission, and absorption) as they interact with various materials (e.g., lenses, mirrors, and prisms).

7DC1761A10C242118E03BE8E96FBF9F1.description: Investigate research-based mechanisms for capturing and converting wave energy (frequency, amplitude, wavelength, and speed) into electrical energy.

DBF575AFBFE7468E871FF6E203C89CE5.description: Collect, organize, and interpret data about the characteristics of sound and light waves to construct explanations about the relationship between matter and energy.

CF9F529486DF4D1BAC8ADBA46B8263FA.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the properties, behaviors, and application of waves.

860F3D7974B04D65AE4A8830B178E61C.description: Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare and contrast embryological and homologous/analogous structures across multiple species to identify evolutionary relationships.

5D05BF33325A4436BE2EC52B156A6FD1.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to explain that separated populations, that remain separated, can evolve through mutations to become a new species (speciation).

2AC9018CA18D4B8BA9F7CC3AEEE0E25A.description: Construct written and verbal explanations to describe how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some organisms' probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.

37C6A931236344BA9978973FF5D37289.description: Analyze and interpret data (e.g. pictures, graphs) to explain how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.

14572F6D1A3D4320902E77ACE2B19CF8.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how similarities and differences among living and extinct species provide evidence that changes have occurred in organisms over time and that similarity of characteristics provides evidence of common ancestry.

9D624923B2074A23A186BE50AB81CFB5.description: Investigate to construct explanations about natural selection that connect growth, survival, and reproduction to genetic factors, environmental factors, food intake, and interactions with other organisms.

72092E28BAF04177A6BED6DB3475B03D.description: Use various scientific resources to analyze the historical findings of Charles Darwin to explain basic principles of natural selection.

EF4E2CC5FEDE4D6CA340DE5C7EA6FC5F.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the process of natural selection, in which variations in a population increase some individuals' likelihood of surviving and reproducing in a changing environment.

D4C3E7DDF8E14D00B30DD60F54AB5BFD.description: Construct scientific arguments from evidence to support claims about the potentially harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects of genetic mutations on organisms.

E9BB1CFB860E42F18F06CF9C5237B79C.description: Communicate through diagrams that chromosomes contain many distinct genes and that each gene holds the instructions for the production of specific proteins, which in turn affects the traits of the individual (not to include transcription or translation).

D5B1E1475DCA4BACB2AA305A3FB3115C.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that chromosomes contain many distinct genes and that each gene holds the instructions for the production of a specific protein, which in turn affects the traits of an individual.

B92BC90FE62B4A7895D004673E8D5103.description: Debate the ethics of artificial selection (selective breeding, genetic engineering) and the societal impacts of humans changing the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.

A706B1CBB4AB455DBAD4BE324AEE6C10.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to analyze data and make predictions about the outcome of specific genetic crosses (monohybrid Punnett Squares) involving simple dominant/recessive traits.

B3D3C241243A4B53842A00368721B713.description: Use various scientific resources to research and support the historical findings of Gregor Mendel to explain the basic principles of heredity.

956287AECD9E48AF8693FEB7110862F3.description: Construct an argument based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.

A783C9A1CE69441C950932C257E14D8E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the differences in inherited and acquired characteristics and how environmental factors (natural selection) and the use of technologies (selective breeding, genetic engineering) influence the transfer of genetic information.

7202AF0859154768B636AE4D01531EDF.description: Compare and contrast advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction.

9E9B449FAE244DE0925EF26E73F6BD37.description: Engage in discussion using models and evidence to explain that sexual reproduction produces offspring that have a new combination of genetic information different from either parent.

FB5C081C85B94F25A2D523E416F561DB.description: Construct explanations of how genetic information is transferred during meiosis.

E124EA411E2B4F4D96FE1681BB72E8C6.description: Create a diagram of mitosis and explain its role in asexual reproduction, which results in offspring with identical genetic information.

4D16705FEFC2474FB78B6075DDCDB53A.description: Obtain and communicate information about the relationship of genes, chromosomes, and DNA, and construct explanations comparing their relationship to inherited characteristics.

7156C748E2A14902A6FE9C4E26D88DB0.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation while asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

5FBBCB85BDA24D288C37FC2F7AB0BCDC.description: Design a process for cleaning a polluted environment (e.g., simulating an oil spill in the ocean or a flood in a city and creating a solution for containment and/or cleanup). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the environment.

267D6561FDB849149D2B7B791067867F.description: Use maps and historical information to identify natural resources in the state connecting (a) how resources are used for human needs and (b) how the use of those resources impacts the environment.

C7A6D09503084976999A8CA1A76F581D.description: Obtain and communicate information to exemplify how humans attain, use, and protect renewable and nonrenewable Earth resources.

88FBD82B7BAF48F38AAA7AB5086BFCFF.description: Identify some of Earth's resources that are used in everyday life such as water, wind, soil, forests, oil, natural gas, and minerals and classify as renewable or nonrenewable.

C6CD68969764457EAE11C8B58EC3067A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that all materials, energy, and fuels that humans use are derived from natural sources.

528B4FD3F5BB48459710105F56C1C9B3.description: Use graphical representations to communicate the distribution of freshwater and saltwater on Earth (e.g., oceans, lakes, rivers, glaciers, groundwater, or polar ice caps).

F5CBDB7611B24F309C449025C802141F.description: Construct explanations of how different landforms and surface features result from the location and movement of water on Earth's surface (e.g., watersheds, drainage basins, deltas, or rivers).

275F30DFE878472D878AC1D2A94B0551.description: Develop models to communicate the characteristics of the Earth's major systems, including the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere (e.g., digital models, illustrations, flip books, diagrams, charts, tables).

73890AB5206B4572A8A0049FCA6C4460.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how the Earth's systems (i.e., geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere) interact in multiple ways to affect Earth's surface materials and processes.

C4B923CC62ED4EF5BD81A049B05583D8.description: Compare and contrast constructive (e.g., deposition, volcano) and destructive (e.g., weathering, erosion, earthquake) processes of the Earth.

246D88E69D2A43F8ABEEA20C2916B4F2.description: Develop and use models of weathering, erosion, and deposition processes which explain the appearance of various Earth features (e.g., the Grand Canyon, Arches National Park in Utah, Plymouth Bluff in Columbus, or Red Bluff in Marion County, Mississippi).

B47B51F70EEA49C5B62636C248489FAA.description: Develop and use models to describe the characteristics of Earth's continental landforms and classify landforms as volcanoes, mountains, valleys, canyons, planes, and islands.

C542FFC8CD56407DB07F1AEA6960C368.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information (e.g. using technology) to describe the four major layers of Earth and the varying compositions of each layer.

BF19AE18376D4124AA972EFBEBFFCFA4.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the composition of Earth and the processes which change Earth's landforms.

1F0DC62124BB4993AABC75A26070844B.description: Ask questions to generate testable hypotheses regarding the formation and location of fossil types, including their presence in some sedimentary rock.

C635E29C8DCF47A5AAD393B3C48BC764.description: Develop and use models to demonstrate the processes involved in the development of various rock formations, including superposition, and how those formations can fracture and move over time.

404DDBF56AD6403686472EF17740784A.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to identify the processes involved in forming the three major types of rock, and investigate common techniques used to identify them.

5770496B7CF44F3E8F31AAB0CF501ECD.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the various processes involved in the rock cycle, superposition of rock layers, and fossil formation.

1E7107057DC04A38924D84B45A609C26.description: Define and solve a simple design problem by applying scientific ideas about magnets (e.g., can opener, door latches, paperclip holders, finding studs in walls, magnetized paint). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the magnet.

59D1C2AC19424F06A5A81679E5DB2D15.description: Research and communicate information to explain how magnets are used in everyday life.

0FE92BB16C29436A867667DE2752F1B9.description: Plan an experiment to investigate the relationship between a force applied to an object (e.g., friction, gravity) and resulting motion of the object.

EE20E9C55A4E4A57B1C2FC9AFE82F6FE.description: Compare and contrast the effects of different strengths and directions of forces on the motion of an object (e.g., gravity, polarity, attraction, repulsion, or strength).

D979416E36A341308637DF706DF7683A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of magnets and the effects of pushes, pulls, and friction on the motion of objects.

DFF0F8E2FC4747539715A22AFFDFD10F.description: Plan and conduct investigations that particles speed up or slow down with addition or removal of heat.

BC9C4BE8954643BD8CDCE70B55373E0F.description: Develop and use models to communicate the concept that matter is made of particles too small to be seen that move freely around in space (e.g., inflation and shape of a balloon, wind blowing leaves, or dust suspended in the air).

5D1BCF7465484832A75B2DB299FBC794.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to determine how changes in heat (i.e., an increase or decrease) change matter from one state to another (e.g., melting, freezing, condensing, boiling, or evaporating).

7398D59461DC463AA7DB6F718063DA6D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the physical properties of matter to explain why matter can change states between a solid, liquid, or gas dependent upon the addition or removal of heat.

5E510716474648019F74C271D350855C.description: Organization of Matter and Chemical Interactions

8E4966A3B61D45C29DE0B5A7388378ED.description: Construct scientific argument using evidence from fossils of plants and animals that lived long ago to infer the characteristics of early environments (e.g., marine fossils on dry land, tropical plant fossils in arctic areas, or fossils of extinct organisms in any environment).

4454D5BE0D6E4D9DBF9A6D2F6D2BEAEC.description: Define and improve a solution to a problem created by environmental changes and any resulting impacts on the types of density and distribution of plant and animal populations living in the environment (e.g., replanting sea oats in coastal areas or developing or preserving wildlife corridors and green belts). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the environment.

352BA447741F4228BCD7DD8FB1CD0BCA.description: Analyze and interpret data to explain how variations in characteristics among organisms of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing (e.g., plants with larger thorns being less likely to be eaten by predators or animals with better camouflage colorations being more likely to survive and bear offspring).

824FEB1D951A4FC29215603F645AEC14.description: Ask questions to predict how natural or man-made changes in a habitat cause plants and animals to respond in different ways, including hibernating, migrating, responding to light, death, or extinction (e.g., sea turtles, the dodo bird, or nocturnal species).

0891689EC3BE45F28150A11B4CE4F8D0.description: Obtain data from informational text to explain how changes in habitats (both those that occur naturally and those caused by organisms) can be beneficial or harmful to the organisms that live there.

36F6CE00269B41418C96CFAE440265AD.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how adaptations allow animals to satisfy life needs and respond both physically and behaviorally to their environment.

D015F5990C0A4B0EA7A55ABF8F9CDEC9.description: Research to justify the concept that traits can be influenced by the environment (e.g., stunted growth in normally tall plants due to insufficient water, changes in an arctic fox's fur color due to light and/or temperature, or flamingo plumage).

4C6B6057243B4E9DA8FF792F77FC49E4.description: Obtain and communicate data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from both parent organisms and that variations of these traits exist in groups of similar organisms (e.g., flower colors in pea plants or fur color and pattern in animal offspring).

F6811DE70AFE413E8AE6D9EBECCBCC46.description: Describe and provide examples of offspring from two parent organisms as containing a combination of inherited traits from both parent organisms.

383442170F014E0B8898DC053F3CD182.description: Describe and provide examples of plant and animal offspring from a single parent organism (e.g., bamboo, fern, or starfish) as being an exact replica with identical traits as the parent organism.

C7D1B2ED366C4CB3AFDDF6DD7471E4C5.description: Identify traits and describe how traits are passed from parent organism(s) to offspring in plants and animals.

645C95393FB94B11B39D13DD62907752.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that through reproduction, the survival and physical features of plants and animals are inherited traits from parent organisms but can also be influenced by the environment.

AECE93BBFCC3438FBC2E3DE4CAF61916.description: Obtain and communicate examples of physical features or behaviors of vertebrates and invertebrates and how these characteristics help them survive in particular environments (e.g., animals hibernate, migrate, or estivate to stay alive when food is scarce or temperatures are not favorable).

4D517448B8C648E5A2562345CA437C78.description: Examine evidence to communicate information that the internal and external structures of plant (e.g., thorns, leaves, stems, roots, or colored petals) function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction

55DBC6F80D054DD785D1FBE0A98CAC76.description: Examine evidence to communicate information that the internal and external structures of animals (e.g., heart, stomach, bone, lung, brain, skin, ears, appendages) function to support survival, growth, and behavior.

FBF713685A324517A75F571E48AC8F4A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of internal and external structures in plants and animals and how they relate to their growth, survival, behavior, and reproduction within an environment.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

CD6D91FB098E4C65B1EDB01C55F233DF.description: Design a process for better preparing communities to withstand manmade or natural disasters (e.g., removing oil from water or soil, systems that reduce the impact of floods, structures that resist hurricane forces). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the disaster plan.

CC67A47104E14CE6A9E0D46A86ACCE50.description: Collect and organize scientific ideas that individuals and communities can use to conserve Earth's natural resources and systems (e.g., implementing watershed management practices to conserve water resources, utilizing no-till farming to improve soil fertility, reducing emissions to abate air pollution, or recycling to reduce landfill waste).

0037C679F7784DF7970BB88809771CD5.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the effects of human interaction with Earth and how Earth's natural resources can be protected and conserved.

2C44DFA27EB249BB8FE86C257C7DDD15.description: Obtain information and analyze how our understanding of the solar system has evolved over time (e.g., Earth-centered model of Aristotle and Ptolemy compared to the Sun-centered model of Copernicus and Galileo).

63E271AFB70C45B3B35EFE1DD41D51C5.description: Develop and use models to explain the factors (e.g., tilt, revolution, and angle of sunlight) that result in Earth's seasonal changes.

75A50A058CFF44B29E327946C33DC67E.description: Develop and use a model of the Earth-Sun-Moon system to analyze the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, solar and lunar eclipses, and seasons.

603FBAB23EBD486B928B3F767DBCB81D.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and research (e.g., from NASA, NOAA, or the USGS) to explain patterns in the location, movement, and appearance of the moon throughout a month and over the course of a year.

C1B6533A4EBB43A08F47BF43A3512938.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the principles that govern moon phases, day and night, appearance of objects in the sky, and seasonal changes.

29F39C76E74E45C0BA310575CC54E8D5.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims about the importance of astronomy in navigation and exploration, including the use of telescopes, compasses, and star charts.

D44FC2FAFD9946CCA09B2D5BB553EDEC.description: Describe how constellations appear to move from Earth's perspective throughout the seasons (e.g., Ursa Major, Ursa Minor, and Orion).

113AC84BE6B24006A804460E9317E62B.description: Use evidence to argue why the sun appears brighter than other stars.

66837C0730224B628191C6F56D2D7D2D.description: Develop and use scaled models of Earth's solar system to demonstrate the size, composition (i.e., rock or gas), location, and order of the planets as they orbit the Sun.

77B22E4E19F2427A862EE39150955F91.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the locations of objects in the universe.

F850A189904947E3937D0296E7216E1E.description: Design a system to increase the effects of friction on the motion of an object (e.g., non-slip surfaces or vehicle braking systems or flaps on aircraft wings). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the system.

700762050BA74F868B717D31E44220EB.description: Predict how a change of force, mass, and/or friction affects the motion of an object to convert potential energy into kinetic energy.

9A0DB7BF52D349159674D6EF85D7F98F.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to test the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the speed and/or direction of objects in motion.

DD8FA99DBA0545518E55E7A5E67BE962.description: Develop and use models to explain how the amount or type of force, both contact and non-contact, affects the motion of an object.

8272BD78FDB34C6FBDF26337856C740F.description: Predict the future motion of various objects based on past observation and measurement of position, direction, and speed.

71F7F19A7ADD43DB8495950754503CA5.description: Obtain and communicate information describing gravity's effect on an object.

F9731761AADA4DD9BAD10FC5C273BFCB.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the factors that affect the motion of an object through a study of Newton's Laws of Motion.

8168B8267BD049F6BCD7E99335C98826.description: Analyze and interpret data to support claims that when two substances are mixed, the total weight of matter is conserved.

6732F42CF3B64EB0A0BFD3E88F148C58.description: Analyze and communicate the results of physical changes to a substance that results in a reversible change (e.g., changes in states of matter with the addition or removal of energy, changes in size or shape, or combining/separating mixtures or solutions).

E02A0F067EC94F3682207A79AE11D1A9.description: Analyze and communicate the results of chemical changes that result in the formation of new materials (e.g., decaying, burning, rusting, or cooking).

FA5F21B9FD484F03A65BBC81C203C19D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the difference between physical and chemical changes.

4C7C7AB344534EDE90B1025B1D2BECFE.description: Design an effective system (e.g., sifting, filtration, evaporation, magnetic attraction, or floatation) for separating various mixtures. Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the system.

69A61836F4A84D4AA4AEB60EE0EC8362.description: Investigate how different variables (e.g., temperature change, stirring, particle size, or surface area) affect the rate at which a solute will dissolve.

8DE0849885CA4BE8A0C1597D2279D648.description: Analyze and interpret data to communicate that the concentration of a solution is determined by the relative amount of solute versus solvent in various mixtures.

6B615EEB053C40CC86DF910C8A363F58.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to describe what happens to the properties of substances in mixtures and solutions.

0B28BE4C274A43B486F7B76238327289.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of mixtures and solutions.

98CDB4DDDC624C8A835BFCE8160A8DBC.description: Design a vessel that can safely transport a dense substance (e.g., syrup, coins, marbles) through water at various distances and under variable conditions. Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the vessel.

F08B062E9B0141D4B7EE524FF678BDF8.description: Make and test predictions about how the density of an object affects whether the object sinks or floats when placed in a liquid.

2B6A86480F6F4CB9833BFFD82FFA1713.description: Analyze matter through observations and measurements to classify materials (e.g., powders, metals, minerals, or liquids) based on their properties (e.g., color, hardness, reflectivity, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, response to magnetic forces, solubility, or density).

A0DD7256CA13446F93FEBAC1B537EF9C.description: Collect, analyze, and interpret data from measurements of the physical properties of solids, liquids, and gases (e.g., volume, shape, movement, and spacing of particles).

548656E54DC94CD7B73D667207BFC606.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to describe basic physical properties of atoms and molecules.

586D24E9306D472CBDF65EE6B052534E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the physical properties of matter.

A27EFF95C9704BC7A23C8DBF23C52443.description: Organization of Matter and Chemical Interactions

77D18209C745441DBCBD3028C10935F3.description: Communicate scientific or technical information that explains human positions in food webs and our potential impacts on these systems.

21C058B293F74AABA0830A32DFAC29DC.description: Design and interpret models of food webs to justify what effects the removal or the addition of a species (i.e., introduced or invasive) would have on a specific population and/or the ecosystem as a whole.

4F01EF8F0F4C42DAB63D78C3A3296D8F.description: Develop and use a food chain model to classify organisms as producers, consumers, or decomposers. Trace the energy flow to explain how each group of organisms obtains energy.

9FA5EE5568AA430DB61EE42CFB7ADAFA.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information regarding the characteristics of different ecosystems and the organisms they support (e.g., salt and fresh water, deserts, grasslands, forests, rain forests, or polar tundra lands).

5E3A061174084A33A4489D70416AEF6A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of a healthy ecosystem with a stable web of life and the roles of living things within a food chain and/or food web, including producers, primary and secondary consumers, and decomposers.

AD0692003ABB4C9B9D5ADC162FF10182.description: Analyze environments that do not receive direct sunlight and devise explanations as to how photosynthesis occurs, either naturally or artificially.

DDBCF9557A61456A9B5E8E1B931BB2B2.description: Research and communicate the basic process of photosynthesis that is used by plants to convert light energy into chemical energy that can be stored and released to fuel an organism's activities.

658679F7F77A4D87B142F3A3BA98FABB.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of photosynthesis and the transfer of energy from the sun into chemical energy necessary for plant growth and survival.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

088ADB074EC241DAAC5F7D1CFBD78A1E.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to investigate and model current technological uses of biomimicry to address solutions to real-world problems.

7F3BEF5DE9DC448EB0F23E9CE6AE451C.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to create a solution that addresses changing ecological conditions (e.g., climate change, invasive species, loss of biodiversity, human population growth, habitat destruction, biomagnification, or natural phenomena).

0E19C889B01041539CC86BB86612697A.description: Investigate and evaluate factors involved in primary and secondary ecological succession using local, real world examples.

B1917D4F4A584570B2FED4694526A262.description: Analyze and interpret population data, both density-dependent and density-independent, to define limiting factors. Use graphical representations (growth curves) to illustrate the carrying capacity within ecosystems.

19E19F4C40FA43299BDA8137FF93FE60.description: Evaluate symbiotic relationships (e.g., mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism) and other co-evolutionary (e.g., predator-prey, cooperation, competition, and mimicry) relationships within specific environments.

1DC8E6975A064A84B5838E30F737E50A.description: Develop and use models to describe the flow of energy and amount of biomass through food chains, food webs, and food pyramids.

07057ED346C64DBBAE5A8B61D26E682B.description: Analyze and interpret quantitative data to construct an explanation for the effects of greenhouse gases on the carbon dioxide cycle and global climate.

EC27CE95F5254BDE86FD5F515946B170.description: Analyze models of the cycling of matter (e.g., carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and water) between abiotic and biotic factors in an ecosystem and evaluate the ability of these cycles to maintain the health and sustainability of the ecosystem.

2E2377330A6A4ED0B3B14FB8E65658C9.description: Illustrate levels of ecological hierarchy, including organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome, and biosphere.

0F000C449B22477FAC6B29DEA205DF8F.description: Students will Investigate and evaluate the interdependence of living organisms and their environment.

B6007511FCD14AA898458844B644E10B.description: Interdependence of Organisms and Their Environments

291F664540204AC3B87FF53D0EAE2870.description: Enrichment: Construct explanations for how various disease agents (bacteria, viruses, chemicals) can influence natural selection.

016950F556C64007A0DB64B17D254105.description: Construct explanations for the mechanisms of speciation (e.g., geographic and reproductive isolation).

CB0259CB35EA4CB88E63E9C2056FF63A.description: Use Darwin's Theory to explain how genetic variation, competition, overproduction, and unequal reproductive success acts as driving forces of natural selection and evolution.

10652AABF0DC4956BE7289104CCD792F.description: Design models and use simulations to investigate the interaction between changing environments and genetic variation in natural selection leading to adaptations in populations and differential success of populations.

696DEF546EE0410DAB695D2ED35B134F.description: Construct cladograms/phylogenetic trees to illustrate relatedness between species.

3404C88674FA4128943DD46EB6B30964.description: Evaluate empirical evidence of common ancestry and biological evolution, including comparative anatomy (e.g., homologous structures and embryological similarities), fossil record, molecular/biochemical similarities (e.g., gene and protein homology), and biogeographic distribution.

168A3DA577A845A288F6BBE1B33E8D57.description: Use models to differentiate between organic and chemical evolution, illustrating the steps leading to aerobic heterotrophs and photosynthetic autotrophs.

3AD46B49C49F4CFCA6393391C9F0591F.description: Students will analyze and interpret evidence to explain the unity and diversity of life.

681D8CFB6D6249DCBED4546BB8D2B93F.description: Enrichment: Investigate current biotechnological applications in the study of the genome (e.g., transcriptome, proteome, individualized sequencing, and individualized gene therapy).

5C51FC6E9FEB4649A6EE9E72C9500F34.description: Research and identify how DNA technology benefits society. Engage in scientific argument from evidence over the ethical issues surrounding the use of DNA technology (e.g., cloning, transgenic organisms, stem cell research, and the Human Genome Project, gel electrophoresis).

23604CA5F3774FA2992F2155E7C7C5D3.description: Use models to predict how various changes in the nucleotide sequence (e.g., point mutations, deletions, and additions) will affect the resulting protein product and the subsequent inherited trait.

0E4F8EAC35B54FE1AD65E10E94545348.description: Evaluate the mechanisms of transcription and translation in protein synthesis.

6A532A2CD0ED457B983FA0D9F5D6731C.description: Develop and use models to explain the relationship between DNA, genes, and chromosomes in coding the instructions for the traits transferred from parent to offspring.

85D6202A147347C1879EAA0C3BAC7A84.description: Students will construct an explanation based on evidence to describe how the structure and nucleotide base sequence of DNA determines the structure of proteins or RNA that carry out essential functions of life.

521B421B3945434A9EA47CD372BE3D32.description: Analyze and interpret data (e.g., pedigrees, family, and population studies) regarding Mendelian and complex genetic traits (e.g., sickle-cell anemia, cystic fibrosis, muscular dystrophy, color-blindness, and hemophilia) to determine patterns of inheritance and disease risk.

0FA6950EA706411AB7CE3ABCAA8CA806.description: Investigate traits that follow non-Mendelian inheritance patterns (e.g., incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles in human blood types, and sex-linkage).

8769F8E255454308A419476250A9BB3F.description: Illustrate Mendel's law of independent assortment using Punnett squares and/or the product rule of probability to analyze monohybrid crosses.

6E04EC1550C446FC8C362BAD64E3F88A.description: Demonstrate Mendel's law of dominance and segregation using mathematics to predict phenotypic and genotypic ratios by constructing Punnett squares with both homozygous and heterozygous allele pairs.

21ABE1B3E92B44CFB615C08E8FD78A8F.description: Students will analyze and interpret data collected from probability calculations to explain the variation of expressed traits within a population.

D5BB42232DB64E68B3A0D25BA4C1699C.description: Investigate chromosomal abnormalities (e.g., Down syndrome, Turner's syndrome, and Klinefelter syndrome) that might arise from errors in meiosis (nondisjunction) and how these abnormalities are identified (karyotypes).

1589DC3D9A7948F1B72605F7532A7B00.description: Compare and contrast mitosis and meiosis in terms of reproduction.

C6F449A89ACB4047916779F95B0A9706.description: Model sex cell formation (meiosis) and combination (fertilization) to demonstrate the maintenance of chromosome number through each generation in sexually reproducing populations. Explain why the DNA of the daughter cells is different from the DNA of the parent cell.

6D56385DF6D14784A8D4D1DF2F3FE297.description: Students will develop and use models to explain the role of meiosis in the production of haploid gametes required for sexual reproduction.

67B4BF8A15AE4F19B4833BD6A3C3E57F.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to manipulate factors involved in fermentation to optimize energy production.

D6720A9FAE364901A54B328E1DF4F30A.description: Enrichment: Investigate variables (e.g., nutrient availability, temperature) that affect anaerobic respiration and current real-world applications of fermentation.

2C9428FEC46C40C1B4DD48AAAA58B80B.description: Conduct scientific investigations or computer simulations to compare aerobic and anaerobic cellular respiration in plants and animals, using real world examples.

EE004AF198FD4226A32F07F132AF223D.description: Develop models of the major reactants and products of cellular respiration (aerobic and anaerobic) to demonstrate the transformation of the chemical energy stored in food to the available energy of ATP. Emphasize the chemical processes in which bonds are broken and energy is released, and new bonds are formed and energy is stored.

B9CC4D564D1F45529AE5F54E520AA2F4.description: Develop models of the major reactants and products of photosynthesis to demonstrate the transformation of light energy into stored chemical energy in cells. Emphasize the chemical processes in which bonds are broken and energy is released, and new bonds are formed and energy is stored.

CEC52F39622243BB9086A0E8CBA3D862.description: Use models to demonstrate that ATP and ADP are cycled within a cell as a means to transfer energy.

F8ACDE8FDACC467EACED5CEBC76D90A8.description: Students will explain that cells transform energy through the processes of photosynthesis and cellular respiration to drive cellular functions.

F85C3A79E5304084BDF36FA2D0A62242.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to investigate the role of stem cells in regeneration and asexual reproduction, then develop applications of stem cell research to solve human medical conditions.

BB7481477EDD4AFABDA66F2FDA1EF16E.description: Relate the processes of cellular reproduction to asexual reproduction in simple organisms (i.e., budding, vegetative propagation, regeneration, binary fission). Explain why the DNA of the daughter cells is the same as the parent cell.

0A047B2489C34F89BD3D6DEFE873E90F.description: Identify and describe the changes that occur in a cell during replication. Explore problems that might occur if the cell does not progress through the cycle correctly (cancer).

9056C710102946CD890D4C326D1BF4C2.description: Construct models to explain how the processes of cell division and cell differentiation produce and maintain complex multicellular organisms.

7D6A588DC9EB4668B34679DAFA9D7F12.description: Students will develop and use models to explain the role of the cell cycle during growth, development, and maintenance in multicellular organisms.

654290D29DB242C88178D567470A6337.description: Develop and use models to explain how the cell deals with imbalances of solute concentration across the cell membrane (i.e., hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic conditions, sodium/potassium pump).

B4FD07F41DB54552A3BB0411D33453DC.description: Plan and conduct investigations to prove that the cell membrane is a semi-permeable, allowing it to maintain homeostasis with its environment through active and passive transport processes.

3F41C48CE83C4149A1F6BBDFE6DCEAE4.description: Students will describe the structure of the cell membrane and analyze how the structure is related to its primary function of regulating transport in and out of cells to maintain homeostasis.

0973497F3CCB41EFB2F0019BA7D9ADCA.description: Contrast the structure of viruses with that of cells, and explain why viruses must use living cells to reproduce.

84E780CB58F843F18A9754AC393AE56E.description: Investigate to compare and contrast prokaryotic cells and eukaryotic cells, and plant, animal, and fungal cells.

246A5F0D8B2A4D188A658A9DD0F5CC0D.description: Develop and use models to explore how specialized structures within cells (e.g., nucleus, cytoskeleton, endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, mitochondria, chloroplast, centrosomes, and vacuoles) interact to carry out the functions necessary for organism survival.

FE6F5ED7F91C444FA07C617A1495E047.description: Students will relate the diversity of organelles to a variety of specialized cellular functions.

43238C50E034406EA34E40EF1DF38F11.description: Design and conduct an experiment to determine how enzymes react given various environmental conditions (i.e., pH, temperature, and concentration). Analyze, interpret, graph, and present data to explain how those changing conditions affect the enzyme activity and the rate of the reactions that take place in biological organisms.

649AC19281A74D5DA937346A5DF7E209.description: Develop and use models to compare and contrast the structure and function of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) in organisms.

4F7438A135E74D8694EA1AA4E41A7208.description: Students will analyze the structure and function of the macromolecules that make up cells.

58B15A3104274AB7A16A9C47DFBC7F5E.description: Use evidence from current scientific literature to support whether a virus is living or non-living.

7FC6B955776D4479955EC49C58F7E800.description: Using specific examples, explain how cells can be organized into complex tissues, organs, and organ systems in multicellular organisms.

1C8C8B166C324F4D9DA7F1868ECA8B9F.description: Describe the tenets of cell theory and the contributions of Schwann, Hooke, Schleiden, and Virchow.

0541FC40A29649879B7CE5377C375FCC.description: Develop criteria to differentiate between living and non-living things.

1E052C2B83794339ACD23CC511F340AA.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics of life and biological organization.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

1EF7F17848B54CBCA73B4963944B5F1E.description: Create a device that will collect free water to meet a human need (e.g., household drinking water, watering plants/animals, cleaning). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the device.

3D9D4D79E011449994D6090D87396AA7.description: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the use and quality of water in the local environment.

8814C179C82D4DA8A8C600142DC44636.description: Obtain and evaluate informational texts and other media to generate and answer questions about water sources and human uses of clean water.

EA4B3E8860544E068209CE04A661F245.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of human dependence on clean and renewable water resources.

9548EED043F04BDABE3E1288F079432E.description: With teacher guidance, plan and conduct a structured investigation to determine how the movement of water can change the shape of the land on earth.

C08507FC42C244C3912B8A605A4A6DA5.description: Generate and answer questions to explain the patterns and location of frozen and liquid bodies of water on earth using maps, globes, or other media.

9A94DDB26C644F60808AC084FDCE9D4B.description: Locate, classify, and describe bodies of water (oceans, rivers, lakes, and ponds) on the Earth's surface using maps, globes, or other media.

D815A61210A84A38B16576D56C3F41B3.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of models (drawings or maps) to describe how water and land are distributed on Earth.

924E6D546B1C4614B67C622382DC1047.description: Obtain and communicate information about severe weather conditions to explain why certain safety precautions are necessary.

D60972D8AD0F4DBCB0CD437D71F10B11.description: Construct an explanation for the general pattern of change in daily temperatures by measuring and calculating the difference between morning and afternoon temperatures.

B4470B88655E4B64A6C5DA1B1C3810CF.description: Develop and use models to predict weather conditions associated with seasonal patterns and changes.

D098D8D87365472FBC8C3A2D47DA4ED3.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to describe local weather conditions (including temperature, wind, and forms of precipitation).

06D5881C17B343AE9E601FEFCB1ADA3B.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the patterns of weather by describing, recording, and analyzing weather data to answer questions about daily and seasonal weather patterns.

F3FAC7D0E0ED45908169A38325B99044.description: Create a device that uses light and/or sound to communicate over a distance (e.g., signal lamp with a flashlight). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the device.

16D5D1C352014C34ADE44FB58C963F03.description: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that vibrations create sound (e.g., pluck a guitar string) and that sound can create vibrations (e.g., feeling sound through a speaker).

E102FE8B430E48A983F57682E4EEF537.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of sound.

57D645CE980B4A47A5C05FB50BBC09C0.description: Use evidence from observations to explain how shadows form and change with the position of the light source.

399DDFCFEDA448468F6894274D9F1A47.description: Construct explanations using first-hand observations or other media to describe how reflected light makes an object visible.

F3A5D657CB084B8490D3A1F4F88F701D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding that light is required to make objects visible.

FFF94C8434474FC5B6A0C7B6FEE1BD9E.description: Create a solution for an agricultural problem (i.e. pollination, seed dispersal, over-crowding). Use an engineering design process to define the problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve the solution.

F43624E579704EE5A65B6D1D54AA453D.description: Describe how the different characteristics of plants help them to survive in distinct environments (e.g., rain forest, desert, grasslands, forests).

A852DC534B3540058638E36D1EA33324.description: Explore the cause and effect relationship between plant adaptations and environmental changes (i.e., leaves turning toward the sun, leaves changing color, leaves wilting, or trees shedding leaves).

D0E605B09D58473DA8B38FC12FE99AEF.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the ways plants adapt to their environment in order to survive.

9513F647BF034C6D94B1CA907391C433.description: Identify the body parts of a pollinating insect (e.g., bee, butterfly) and describe how insects use these parts to gather nectar or disburse pollen. Report findings using drawings, writing, or models.

BF3FCA43D2954CBFB3FF673365C83AB8.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interdependence of flowering plants and pollinating insects.

E589B3A61D1D45D081E79DA2273596D0.description: Conduct structured investigations to make and test predictions about what plants need to live, grow, and repair including water, nutrients, sunlight, and space. Develop explanations, compare results, and report findings.

B4ED2A6345F946F6A145EAE0BC692580.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of what plants need from the environment for growth and repair.

0688424D52B54F6395EA6D980A40DC44.description: Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information through labeled drawings, the life cycle (egg, larva, pupa, adult) of pollinating insects (e.g., bees, butterflies).

60956E8D40E841808D12B49CC6F30756.description: Investigate, using observations and measurements (non-standard units), flowering plants (pumpkins, peas, marigolds, or sunflowers) as they change during the life cycle (i.e., germination, growth, reproduction, and seed dispersal). Use drawings, writing, or models to communicate findings.

17292CF8C8C54F8DAD1FA4746979E951.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how living things change in form as they go through the general stages of a life cycle.

4BF330A94C294FB2B7CAD5F4652F5E7A.description: With teacher support, gain an understanding that scientists are humans who use observations and experiments to learn about the natural world. Obtain information from informational text or other media about scientists who have made important observations about plants (e.g., Theophrastus, Gregor Mendel, George Washington Carver, Katherine Esau).

EF6F2B1EBD3542DA8CB15D58D643CA14.description: Create a model which explains the function of each plant structure (roots, stem, leaves, petals, flowers, seeds).

68C396C1ED7642309177089D5160CCC7.description: Design and conduct an experiment that shows the absorption of water and how it is transported through the plant. Report observations using drawings, sketches, or models.

11D00C46E95A408B92B296B84791F9E3.description: Obtain information from informational text and other media to describe the function of each plant part (roots absorb water and anchor the plant, leaves make food, the stem transports water and food, petals attract pollinators, flowers produce seeds, and seeds produce new plants).

72CE44167C4840A3BC663057C8C98781.description: Construct explanations using first-hand observations or other media to describe the structures of different plants (i.e., root, stem, leaves, flowers, and fruit). Report findings using drawings, writing, or models.

B9A76D2B804542258427F762496EAA13.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the basic needs and structures of plants.

document.title: Mississippi College and Career Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

09335D0F05954A46A283A6576EADDF01.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5FB06D6871A947CF8B45E3F2BF450946.description: Apply grades 9–10 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

E8D4D0EB0E664269803C78CE6E60A85A.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

2470BB6BFF4F4D39819656CDAE363250.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

A2EADEF812534909BE284B618897900B.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

51FCF06A479E45FB8EF449CE93A95482.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

8C9D0CAF7EE84C05B8B4ECCFBF80640A.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

4C048889A45F477389C22DEBC8ADC9B9.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9AC6829FBD7C482CBAF430044AC2C8DC.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

702CCC52EE994CC6B08EE03175A08087.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

7A598EBDA25F4513B42BD8AFCF7258BF.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole.

903AD5754FB44E02876C4648F5C0D322.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

15DA33D6EE3548029C1941C78CBA3CFC.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

3523EBF149C745C989BF523F4FFFE390.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

08BA7A76D312493FB4ABDAD1FE0540A9.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

F1B06EE405F84174B2E96BC2DDD8D118.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

C0FF4F4EED4E41DBA4CB8EF7B4B0761E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

5DE290EA804B441B86AC11939970BC93.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

CB995037DF924F9081DB450090015413.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

D29F8B86E37045C98B1755B93849F5E6.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

07DB310C7F42459B95E2A54C2C7D5893.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

6B9411C27B9C4AAD9E685D04C8104E05.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

667C968E1E734881B4B46D7B98FD4CBE.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

596EB6E069194F1C8784F97020D0A865.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counter-claims.

2BD1507057D14A3485EAC2A52B5BD367.description: Develop claim(s) and counter-claims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.

6A04EF1AE69E48BBAA58D2B523B5DE3A.description: Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counter-claims, reasons, and evidence.

E7C9AF084BBB4FC0A3617649C894EE1D.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

FFD42DA403FE41738A30475162636B8C.description: By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

E21B0E4FDC2E4466A11D2D570044018B.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

D1A0047B56F34D75B4723E5E66CA4524.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

EFD00A25AC0E453BBBDB976D0F58E771.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

5588EE7C950A46C69D6A568F4E40CA2F.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

23067EFD511D4186A0E373007560963F.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

761C8567058C469DAD2DFB338B87B09C.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

F4C86D8ACD8A40F09A1D7A1912915213.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

24798493DA9242F293B9B8B434348376.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

EA927C3BD487422FA1B614D4E1291BB6.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

1E66D36E5E2543349C62BD712E72CCBD.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.
