0B2E9F407A8848D890F03CEE5B67743A.description: Examine the principles of capitalism as developed by classical economist Adam Smith.

05ACF4A7FD3A4409B345FFB4CC64BB59.description: Results of the Industrial Revolution - Analyze capitalism as the economic philosophy that developed as a result of the Industrial Revolution and compare economic reactions to capitalism including socialism and communism.

1C9809D9A57D4935A578419DCCF07CE6.description: Contrast factors that enhanced or impeded the spread of Industrial Revolution into Eastern Europe and the Far East.

39A29047BE364455ADB1882CB49CD0D8.description: Evaluate important concepts and inventors during the Industrial Revolution (e.g., James Hargreaves, Eli Whitney, James Watt, Thomas Edison, the Bessemer Process, etc.).

F2A517C479224792839C8F937EE8C6AA.description: Discuss the significance of the Agricultural Revolution, Enclosure Movement, and the Industrial Revolution and their impact on society (e.g., Charles Townshend, John Deere, Cyrus McCormick, etc.).

0D96ACA0FF09441780A758A548261437.description: Analyze the factors that led to the Industrial Revolution in England.

8273877435D046FF90D239FC5E52406B.description: Dawn of the Industrial Revolution - Examine the origins, impact, and spread of the Agricultural and Industrial Revolutions.

4392923F65FB427EBF0EE38C46366EA9.description: Analyze the impact of the revolutionary period on the abolition of the Atlantic slave trade, the Emancipation of Spanish America, and the Issuance of the Monroe Doctrine by the United States.

942710913BA94156AB3667B13B1A351F.description: Evaluate the significant outcomes of the Congress of Vienna and the creation of the Concert of Europe.

B07B430B20D0470CAA19644554C91B90.description: Examine Napoleon's geographic and political influence on Europe through the spread of liberalism and nationalism.

798FCED4C68A4D369E2AFEA91EF0A10A.description: Explain the impact of the American Revolution on the French call for social equality as expressed in the "Declaration of Rights of Man and the Citizen (1789)."

08BC95383D7A4024AC210A2BD3142827.description: Examine various opinions of the developing democratic ideals amidst the economic troubles of the French social class.

45C77341DD5A446193A7670FA2CCC862.description: French Revolution Analyze the causes of the French Revolution and its impact on Europe.

375D99B8873F4E80938988828F1C67E1.description: Differentiate the influence of Charles de Montesquieu, Voltaire, and Jean- Jacques Rousseau on the development of democratic ideals.

D174CFE7FCF54592AACA32B96841AB92.description: Contrast the views of Thomas Hobbes and John Locke concerning the domination of absolute governments.

14D126D3060E4F448C12C9B300FA17AB.description: Compare and contrast new methods of reasoning as demonstrated by Francis Bacon and Rene Descartes (e.g., inductive reasoning and the scientific method, deductive reasoning, etc.).

97E76C1800FC4DA9A46639C781A6FD53.description: Identify the theories of cosmology as described by Nicolaus Copernicus, Galileo Galilei, and Sir Isaac Newton.

CE30A065C215487E9026FD2C40A627FA.description: Scientific Revolution and Enlightenment - Investigate the important ideas and achievements of the Scientific Revolution and the Age of Enlightenment

CB26725EDB804BDDA162F4F910EF551E.description: World History: Age of Enlightenment to Present

C26F3D61910E45C9B43F539D2B595CC4.description: Describe the contributions of various ethnic and religious groups to Mississippi.

396BF8358F0B468FBD9BF900EC5B8BF2.description: Analyze the push and pull factors of people migrating to Mississippi.

FB565D330F9F43C8A663C4BDABC1D95A.description: Cite evidence of the growing ethnic diversity of Mississippi's populations and its impact on the state today.

35B0913900DC4B619FF86F039DDE584C.description: Identify and describe the various ethnic and religious groups in Mississippi.

B9661BD73E4F4D37B053C96515040E37.description: Examine the contributions of various ethnic and religious groups in Mississippi.

56DAFD37C6B84BB1BA8AE2F733E1EE6D.description: Identify locations in Mississippi that have artistic, musical, or literary significance (e.g., Delta-Blues, Coast- Walter Anderson, Jackson- Eudora Welty, etc.).

E8C24857F91A402FB30F96C59B227587.description: Examine the role of cultural diversity in the artistic, musical, and literary traditions of Mississippi.

FF1A1CACFC70450EA49C523507474EE3.description: Analyze how Mississippi's history and/or religious traditions have impacted the state's artist, musicians, and writers.

CF10BB0879E348EF99B711E79F761F71.description: Identify and describe the accomplishments of Mississippi artists, musicians, and writers (e.g., William Faulkner, B.B. King, Muddy Waters, Walter Anderson, Elvis Presley, etc.).

C884C930AD134AD58D7B44CE2ACF8C22.description: Examine the impact of Mississippi artists, musicians, and writers on the state, nation, and world.

2A63681398D3429B9C0D2B788B6D9D12.description: Compare types of services offered by local and state government to meet the needs of Mississippians.

84B8FE3CDBED4FBA9559C8910634CF6A.description: Examine the various forms of local governments and evaluate how they meet the needs of local communities.

BAC3026C1EB94BA78741E64AFAF4591F.description: Analyze the role of the judicial, legislative, and executive branches within the government of Mississippi.

7174F2E391354D7D9721EA73CE516267.description: Evaluate the rights and responsibilities of Mississippi citizenship.

C95C4EB95D8B4207BFDB039BB28CFF9E.description: Analyze the structure and function of local and state government in Mississippi.

249603B8F7314FF181286E0928B31B75.description: Analyze the causes of Mississippi's past and present-day struggle with poverty.

A83E2B84DA9B4B55B9147146854C6E63.description: Analyze how the major industries of Mississippi have impacted the economy in Mississippi.

BC7D87F3063E4CD49FBAC3A4E68AF91A.description: Identify various industries and factories that drive Mississippi's modern economy.

A2FF7E6AC99B478FBA45F7C1C0B09FE0.description: Analyze the economic characteristics of modern Mississippi.

0240B4907B2443AD900EABC79AE6A747.description: Evaluate the lasting impact of the Civil Rights movement on Mississippi.

F390E52F19A6406B9202FD18830FA1BD.description: Examine organized resistance to the Civil Rights Movement in Mississippi and how it shaped the conflict between the State and Federal governments during the Civil Rights Era (e.g., Citizen's Council, MS State Sovereignty Commission, Ross Barnett, etc.).

B254604FA709449A9B550D57BD2AE513.description: Discuss the significant strategies used within the Civil Rights Movement.

B2A4566A863342419C52F39D7F4FDE8A.description: Analyze the significant figures, groups, and events of the Civil Rights Movement in Mississippi (e.g., Emmett Till, Medgar Evers, James Meredith, Fannie Lou Hamer, etc.).

A350CB373A954E168A13F78451DBC25E.description: Evaluate the role of Mississippi in the Civil Rights Movement.

021A1C78542942C18629ECF456A8DEBB.description: Analyze reforms that contributed to social and economic changes after the Civil War (e.g., Jim Crow, poll taxes, literacy tests, segregation, etc.).

EDFD94A6D2CB46008C40996C5059E46F.description: Trace the changes in Mississippi's economy and technology in the decades following Reconstruction.

BB8A83FF317D4A60A4D5AB24ACFC8318.description: Analyze the differences between the Mississippi Constitutions of 1868 and 1890.

788D15DCF5FF4740BF7409B4B4A40412.description: Examine the economic, political, and social changes in the Jim Crow Era Mississippi from the end of Reconstruction through World War II.

DFD8BC67670643AB9E3B1C4FABD24C3A.description: Describe the changing roles and contributions of African American Mississippians during Reconstruction.

CAC904E46CF849C19907EB7911C8421B.description: Analyze the impact of Congressional Reconstruction on Mississippi, including the new Mississippi Constitution of 1868.

7D4CBE57004D4646A3DED7030F265F4C.description: Examine the roles and contributions of women, enslaved people, and free African Americans during the Civil War.

D675B2702B4949C1BB6F03B527FD55D4.description: Analyze the significance of the military campaigns that took place in Mississippi during the Civil War and the impact wartime conditions had on the civilian population.

3B20873F94D84F14951911447C0DD894.description: Examine the Mississippi Declaration of Secession and trace the events that led to the secession of Mississippi from the Union in 1861.

F1B8713FE90C4688AB6A22266640B1DB.description: Analyze the role of Mississippi during the Civil War and evaluate the effects of Reconstruction in the state.

187F15646B274A85BEB492826D922F0B.description: Examine the culture and social structure that developed in Mississippi during the antebellum period.

AA75408B48584DA78D0845CA85664BD7.description: Analyze the relationship between cotton and the evolution of the plantation economy in antebellum Mississippi.

31D978F66D784BD6BC52C82406695EBB.description: Trace the evolution of slavery in Mississippi, including the significance of the Forks of the Road slave market in Natchez.

6BDDDFD65BF249799A125D760CA4C6E7.description: Analyze the characteristics of antebellum Mississippi, with an emphasis on the plantation system and the evolution of slavery.

2FDB03C92A144368AC5F657D0E5F79C0.description: Identify the key points of the Mississippi Constitution of 1817 and identify the government and political influences that led to its development.

7BA332A316A74D6B95E8AC6E35992893.description: Trace the events and legislative processes necessary for Mississippi to gain statehood.

8B16890CAF2A4C6CA515352D69B3CF0A.description: Examine the conflicts ( e.g., Natchez Rebellion, etc.), treaties (e.g., Fort Adams, Mount Dexter, Doak's Stand, Dancing Rabbit Creek, Pontotoc Creek, etc.), and subsequent removal (e.g., Trail of Tears, etc.) of indigenous Mississippians.

00EBA6ED3BBB4AB1AD6A2F19CAA9A710.description: Investigate life and work in Mississippi during the colonial and revolutionary periods.

195795BD45C54301AD9300CBA009C704.description: Explain the development of the Mississippi Territory and its evolution to statehood.

D45A5134B5C444758DB7AF4E812B8445.description: Examine the impact of European arrival and presence on the cultural development of Mississippi (e.g., Code Noir, holiday, religious, economic, etc.).

3CFA191B989547D796639C8847D1ACAA.description: Compare and contrast the French, Spanish and English arrival, and presence in Mississippi (e.g., lifestyles, religion, successes, failures, etc.).

A9A0193C55DC49789612D16F90F2C592.description: Examine the motivations and the effects of the European arrival and presence in Mississippi.

8BBB41D8D6EB42CF8C1626BFD123A992.description: Evaluate the impact of native cultures on Mississippi, past and present.

F260EC725A6442FF85AC691F64B946A8.description: Trace the relationships between the various indigenous groups in Mississippi, including their alliances with the Europeans who settled in what would become the Mississippi Territory.

CD9E86E0889646BC9D6B1A7DE66DA204.description: Explain the impact of Mississippi's geography on the cultural development of its indigenous peoples (e.g., Choctaw, Chickasaw, Natchez, etc.).

4F56C3F2BF414DDF86FF277D011E6D17.description: Compare and contrast the indigenous cultures in Mississippi and assess their lasting impact on the state's history and traditions.

001F53BC8160442C9664BE772000D2DC.description: Explain how the geographic features and processes of Mississippi contribute to social, technological, and economic development throughout the state (e.g., Mississippi River, Gulf Coast, Pine Hills, Delta, Great Flood of 1927, Hurricanes Camille and Katrina, etc.).

AAFE4534A0CC4B758BEEEA5515DB6AED.description: Describe how the geographic and physical features set Mississippi apart from other states.

F56C579ACCD8413AB952E2C27577D272.description: Differentiate among between the geographic regions of Mississippi.

13185942BC5A4C73A596B0DB37B0B1F7.description: Identify the physical features, landforms, and soil regions of Mississippi.

C9102E0505A84D4BBDBC7850D0A3C5A3.description: Examine the geographic features of Mississippi.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

564A7EE22B10429499DEA5FE795701D3.description: Enrichment: Design solutions to reduce the impact of human activity on the ecosystem.

25D6751813074CEDB8BA4B773F1D29C7.description: Engage in scientific argument from evidence to distinguish organisms that exist in symbiotic (mutualism, parasitism, commensalism) or co-evolutionary (predator-prey, cooperation, competition, and mimicry) relationships within ecosystems.

D88FCF48C5C04CF1963C5559F1B50063.description: Use models to analyze the flow of energy through food chains, webs, and pyramids.

5F7464C5BDEA41A1AAB8D9F8CD8762DD.description: Develop and use models to discuss the climate, flora, and fauna of the terrestrial and aquatic biomes of the world.

6832C6AFE80C4FEA8938711FD8B60819.description: Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to explain relationships that exist between abiotic and biotic components of an ecosystem. Explain how changes in biotic and abiotic components affect the balance of an ecosystem over time.

F17CD5D621EA40AB9FFCAB6A91DA3ABD.description: Use models to analyze the cycling of matter in an ecosystem (e.g., water, carbon dioxide/oxygen, nitrogen).

87A6DBC47C0D463F94FC62AEE66B287E.description: Compare and contrast biotic and abiotic factors.

B976820A21B44078A0D7BBE53AFE26CA.description: Students will understand the interdependence of living organisms and their environment.

CCDD4E1232C54FA2B1100A06061F4538.description: Enrichment: Create and analyze models that illustrate the relatedness between all living things (cladograms/phylogenic trees).

3BD4C8043104450D9A0E685CC0521277.description: Investigate how biological adaptations and genetic variations of traits in a population enhance the probability of survival in an environment (natural selection).

96DECB9FD5F04FFF892A0CC5820B461A.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain how DNA evidence and fossil records support Darwin's theory of evolution.

1B03CDBD16214534B0E740E8C0F98910.description: Analyze and interpret data to support claims that different types of fossils provide evidence of the diversity of life that has existed on Earth and of the relationships between past and existing life on Earth.

6EEBF18EDE874DA4B998F58FC05B6A5E.description: Investigate through research the contributions of scientists to the theory of evolution and evolutionary processes (e.g., Needham, Spallanzani, Redi, Pasteur, Lyell, Lamarck, Malthus, Wallace, Darwin).

223DF111EA814DBAA6EBAEA175FDE2AE.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of Earth's fossil record and its indication of the diversity of life over time.

451DFDEFB88B427D8E1FE4E859280266.description: Enrichment: Debate the pros and cons of using biotechnology to manipulate genetic information for human purpose (society).

D94C51CDAC1C44E29EE0525D542FE626.description: Research and report genetic technologies that may improve the quality of life (e.g., genetic engineering, cloning, gene splicing, DNA testing).

C73E96F364F64D7EB3C7CEE0253B293B.description: Obtain and communicate information to describe how mutations may affect genetic expression and provide examples.

4498072FE9A74131BC6D787ABD7F2E1A.description: Use models (e.g., Punnett squares) and mathematical reasoning to describe and predict patterns of inheritance of single genetic traits from parents to offspring (e.g., dominant, and recessive traits, incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, sex- linkage).

4F4B49A9B9194044AFAEAB913811AE01.description: Obtain and communicate information illustrating the relationships among DNA, genes, chromosomes, and proteins to the basis of life.

153534DE09EA453B8DEACE0ACA863E7F.description: Compare and contrast the basic structure and function of nucleic acids (e.g., DNA, RNA).

1F01E20AD3ED45CAA5DBA779E72FD508.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how genetic information is transferred from parent to offspring.

26F397D33916412BB7963426967EB08E.description: Enrichment: Research and orally communicate the possible outcomes of a failure of mitosis (cancer) or meiosis (nondisjunction).

C9B85E0A591E4BC6B0B4529FFB7621E9.description: Compare and contrast the processes and results of mitosis and meiosis.

B45D819691D94F14A1E8A9433E15B685.description: Use models to explain how ADP and ATP cycle to store and release chemical energy using inorganic phosphate.

DAF567E295F04E8B962AEC3FE3BC40B7.description: Analyze the relationship between photosynthesis and cellular respiration and explain that relationship in terms of the need for all living things to acquire energy from their environment.

F943EFF70BE7462AAE2BFF6D6C1694FC.description: Compare and contrast active and passive cellular transport. Analyze the movement of water across a cell membrane in hypotonic, isotonic, and hypertonic solutions.

E9C11FA37D0F4809AEF5A967CF4B6280.description: Use models to investigate and explain structures within living cells that support life (e.g., cytoplasm, cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, lysosomes, Golgi, vacuoles, ER, ribosomes, chromosomes, centrioles, cytoskeleton, nucleolus, nuclear membrane).

9D8EA9F96F914D25916475C020EBE15E.description: Compare and contrast prokaryotic/eukaryotic and plant/animal/bacteria cells.

998039780CE24871A3BEEA2A60F527D2.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how the structure of living organisms supports the essential functions of life.

4304349B855F44229E8B661A3E93E942.description: Organization and Energy in Living Systems

547294D1505E426B8A165B021E45BA63.description: Enrichment: Explore the structure of biomolecules using molecular models. Relate the structure of biomolecules to their function in living things (discuss types bonding, importance of the strength and weakness of the bond in function, energy in bonds, enzyme function).

282C2E8E63514696950BBF7131F62F72.description: Explain the role of the major biomolecules (carbohydrates, proteins -including enzymes, lipids, and nucleic acids) to the survival of living organisms.

53E915D51600432BA4AD1CBC55B59812.description: Investigate how the properties of water (e.g., cohesion, adhesion, heat capacity, solvent properties) contribute to the maintenance of living cells and organisms.

05F525D4BD5041F2AE940E1B973F7705.description: Analyze and interpret data to classify common solutions as acids, bases, or neutral. Communicate the importance of pH in living systems.

75B9D433A7BD48C3B05F3F7ED9BCF343.description: Relate chemical reactivity to an element's position on the periodic table. Use this information to determine what type of bond will form between elements (ionic, covalent, hydrogen).

1803B2EBC4EA49798FD955AF440A728F.description: Obtain and use information about elements (e.g., chemical symbol, atomic number, atomic mass, and group or family) to describe the organization of the periodic table.

562F51630D2746B89DC82371E53999BE.description: Develop and use simple atomic models to describe the components of elements (e.g., relative position, charges of protons, neutrons, and electrons).

531C2B387DCF44669FF2A3BCA2D1B142.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and interactions of matter and how the organization of matter supports living organisms.

0B62178283D647B38D9A79551B8E0854.description: Enrichment: Research, analyze, explain, and communicate the influence of society, including cultural components, on the direction and progress of science and technology (e.g., medical treatments, emerging viruses, antibiotic resistance, vaccinations and re-emergent diseases, alternative energy development, and/or biomimicry.

E3024E0ECB96488C95547685830688D8.description: Research, analyze, explain, and communicate how scientific enterprise relates to society and classic inventions (e.g., microscope, blood typing, gel electrophoresis equipment, DNA sequencing technology).

29E99BB2AC1445DCBE844BA25CE83161.description: Trace and model the historical development of scientific ideas and theories (e.g., creation of the microscope, discovery of cells/cell theory, discovery of DNA/RNA, double helical shape of DNA, evolution/natural selection, endosymbiosis) through the development of a timeline.

387F32D6E8464781A73AF00782968E92.description: Identify and communicate the contributions of famous scientists and their experiments that formed fundamental scientific principles (e.g., Robert Hooke, Schleiden/ Schwann/Virchow, Griffith, Avery/MacLeod/McCarty, Hershey/Chase, Rosalind Franklin, Gregor Mendel, Watson/Crick, Pasteur, and Charles Darwin).

72FF9B3A426F4F23BC6B90BF2F994454.description: Students will relate the importance of significant historical biological experiments and their impact of these on research, development, and society.

49A408B1AFC447A5BE4090FEDF3346C1.description: History of Biology and Impacts on Society

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

8FBFFFDA71AF4B758FE05E27FF7EBCC2.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to define a problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve a societal concern with the aid of plants (e.g., irrigation, water conservation, urban shading, green-space development, food deserts, or other local needs or issues).

EB8A062612004152B198C75A768CEDD4.description: Compare and contrast genomes using plant genetic databases (e.g., BLAST or plant GDB).

BD3F949D90C244D483767A5C85305DB6.description: Conduct transects/plot studies to determine species, biodiversity, or health of a plant community. (Plots may be linear or a quadrat (square or circular) depending on the habitat. (Typically, relative density, relative dominance, and relative frequency of each species are calculated to infer an importance value of the species in the plot.)

B88B25E53010449DA52E3CF9CA33A518.description: Students will ask questions, plan, and conduct field investigations on local plant communities.

BDC5050B66E34BB29145B96B588B0047.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design and build a plant model based on extreme environment criteria to overcome the difficulties presented by this environment. Identify revisions to the proposed model over time.

876141C0E8984665A271550B8141C56E.description: Construct a model using technology that illustrates the levels of succession within a habitat (e.g., graveyard exploration, forest fire area, or reclamation sites).

E9B8C352629A491E8911E457B5C03052.description: Relate atmospheric factors to biodiversity (e.g., climate as determined by temperature and precipitation).

5A404FC0C2E646398041BC4C80C170CE.description: Research plants found in various habitats. Analyze how plants use adaptations for survival in these habitats including extreme habitats.

4B36006403B349829FDB07D71959B802.description: Students will explore adaptations that allow plants to survive in various habitats.

A3C040CBB2614B2B8A2B49C332812B2A.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design and conduct an investigation that uses biomimicry to provide a plant-based solution to an environmental challenge.

A6604AD9DA294BD589CE8DADA9EA6738.description: Explore the impacts (both positive and negative) of plant biotechnology/GMOs on human society. Present findings using digital media or technology, and include evidence using graphs or charts.

3C717D16DCF5491AA7D520DA75CD94CE.description: Investigate the industrial use of plants.

12FD035452074BE9B82D04EB0E0C86C3.description: Investigate historical and modern medicinal uses of plants.

02E8B7DE82EA4DC6AC60BAF2A85348C1.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to define a problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve a habitat impacted by human interactions.

EDD199FA59E647BBBD104EBCC544AF68.description: Identify plants used in the bioremediation of an area due to natural processes (e.g., fire), industrial pollution, or wars, and develop and communicate a plan to remediate a habitat impacted by human interactions (e.g., carbon sinks, phytoremediation, or heavy metal detoxification).

5AC1CAF67D4A4A8F866AD359E14A3FF3.description: Students will explore the global value of plants and the interaction between humans and plants.

1C4575467F094C2E8B0C91CAD984FCEB.description: Using laboratory data, correctly categorize fruits, vegetables, nuts, modified stems, or other plant parts. Compare the scientific definitions of these terms to those used by the general public/society and the USDA to categorize food.

8C4269AA595548B2B8FDCE85D5F9B1CE.description: Plan, conduct, and communicate the results of a comparative laboratory investigation of differing fruit types.

B9C2EB2002194CF7A2D242DAE28B622F.description: Identify differences in flower structure and shape. Provide a rationale that explains the value of these differences in flower structure to reproductive success (e.g., pollinators, flower shape, smell, color, size, orientation).

207793C487354EEBBFCF2BE7530584F3.description: Compare the similarities between corresponding plant reproductive structures from a variety of species. Record via drawings of observed dissection specimens, and explain the similarities and differences observed.

AC8CE4182D09474A943160F9540890EB.description: Plan and conduct comparative flower dissection to identify reproductive structures within the flower.

17836EA4C7A941AC80ABDE22F81655C9.description: Compare and contrast the consequences of the following reproductive methods: asexual reproduction, vegetative propagation, and sexual reproduction.

4F0CF9B9EEB54CAFB1D60D82DBFC1208.description: Enrichment: Research and present an agronomically important crop (e.g., potato, sweet potato, pineapple, or strawberry) that is produced via vegetative propagation (non-GMOs) for human consumption. Include evidence-based arguments that identify the potential benefits and negative effects of this method of crop production.

F810850A4B82428D8E865083B195141D.description: Describe the various processes of asexual reproduction and vegetative propagation used by plants. Communicate the importance of these reproductive methods in regard to human food production.

D284AE300E7745A8BF0BDD3E6D1A3D1D.description: Students will characterize the reproductive strategies of plants.

DE81126B15FB4F93ABDB904CF72F8DC9.description: Enrichment: Referencing the National Center for Biotechnology Information's gene/protein databases, propose and design a scientifically supportable cladogram or phylogenetic tree that illustrates the evolutionary modifications of the plant kingdom using genetic (DNA) or protein sequence comparisons/alignments.

F05F8A52B4F34B5592DCAF3717954A02.description: Research information to develop, produce, and communicate a scientifically justifiable argument for the rapid amplification and success of angiosperm compared to other plant divisions.

6D4E70D2653848A380538F52E05CB4EF.description: Summarize and justify the characteristics of angiosperms and gymnosperms that lead to their success as terrestrial plants.

92BC6635ECEB4B138A0FDF996F22E1F0.description: Referencing the USDA plants database, identify, compare, and contrast seedless, naked seed, and enclosed-seed modifications for reproduction. Calculate the occurrence of seed types in given habitats.

7CF6D94CD2084EF5A02F8E7280D5CB90.description: Summarize and justify the characteristics of nonvascular algae (blue-green and green algae) and bryophytes that provide evidence of evolution within the plant kingdom.

9BA020EDF263453BB033124630B76EBB.description: Students will identify evolutionary modifications necessary for the terrestrial survival of plants.

4211817B7EAA4A8A92702D95752D68EE.description: Compare and contrast functions of the various characteristics found in plant divisions and utilize dichotomous keys to identify plant species.

054B231424A04A26B5BF59B3E7753DE7.description: Identify and compare various live plant examples to explore plant morphological diversity, including leaf number, structure, and arrangement; root modifications; and flower structure and arrangement. Produce a visual product (e.g., an electronic presentation) to identify and communicate patterns of similarity and differences between the lab specimens.

6023925198A2416F9480D569B33E04EE.description: Communicate the importance of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and nitrogen cycles to plant physiology through graphics such as poster or computer presentations.

3979A8CCA4A9449DA711814C63A05555.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to manipulate a variable of choice to refine a protocol to optimize output of photosynthesis or cellular respiration.

F654123961024D9AA09488C9C816A22F.description: Conduct investigations, collect and analyze data, and communicate results that explain the processes of photosynthesis and cellular respiration (e.g., light intensity, light color, light distance, temperature, altering pH, oxygen availability, and carbon dioxide concentration).

71F9B5F96822476EA6A44D2FDDD5E006.description: Demonstrate through model development and manipulation an understanding of plant biochemistry.

CD4FD30C8C0545298914FF37E2F0D233.description: Calculate surface area of leaves/roots, and compare surface areas of various plant specimens to explain adaptations of the various plant types.

72358300CE1643769B1EBB28AFE895F3.description: Evaluate and explain how bacteria and fungi work symbiotically to enhance plant root function.

B5B920D623154E5F8946805A2DA3C88B.description: Describe the relationship between the structure and purpose of plant organs (e.g., roots, stems, and leaves).

7EE784BD28B14455A67541E835EDAC0D.description: Using microscopes, observe, identify, record, and analyze (e.g., see and draw) cells and cell structures unique to plants. Use data measurements obtained from microscopy to compare the plant cells and organelle sizes between various examples (e.g., elodea, onion, or algae).

E1D780434C0F4B63BEC89C56E9A89AF6.description: Analyze models (3-D, paper, and/or computer-based) to distinguish the basic morphology of the plant kingdom, with attention to structures and their related functions. Use cladograms or phylogenetic trees to identify evolutionary features that distinguish the plant kingdom from other kingdoms.

8253B483765D405DBE8110C868CF18DC.description: Students will investigate the morphology, anatomy, and physiology of plants.

0CB4C150458644E18E393AF80E1E55DC.description: Plant Morphology, Cell Structure, and Function

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

0B38F0A751994D579DAA1C7FB71C5C62.description: Enrichment: Investigate parts per million and/or parts per billion as it applies to environmental concerns in your geographic region, and reference laws that govern these factors.

F4B162464F6D4901A8CB4A729112C3D2.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to predict the results of reactions using the concentration of solutions (i.e., solution stoichiometry).

D5A8A16480394D21AE8CE1A2C3CC5F4F.description: Design, conduct, and communicate the results of experiments to produce a specified volume of a solution of a specific molarity, and dilute a solution of a known molarity.

0BD252193CDA4437BEDF7D85D7CFFFF3.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to analyze molarity, molality, dilution, and percentage dilution problems.

F1D15B8A666E4E6BA58976FFB6336D4C.description: Design, conduct, and communicate the results of experiments to test the conductivity of common ionic and covalent compounds in solution.

123A15035FB840EFAFE011268977F803.description: Analyze and interpret data to predict the effect of temperature and pressure on solids and gases dissolved in water.

AEA7AF6A2F4C417FAB59CD1BAB2E254E.description: Develop and use models (e.g., online simulations, games, or video representations) to explain the dissolving process in solvents on the molecular level.

9C9ED774C7EA45149DEA0AAC2F19FE6C.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to quantitatively express the concentration of solutions using the concepts such as molarity, percent by mass, and dilution.

12CE5A311D9E4ED6A86F5FF2F660D144.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the nature of properties of various types of chemical solutions.

1098C96C370A45908A074E407F8D94EA.description: Enrichment: Using gas stoichiometry, calculate the volume of carbon dioxide needed to inflate a balloon to occupy a specific volume. Use an engineering design process to design, construct, evaluate, and improve a simulated air bag.

C7435EDD88DA4A5D814FFF1FFDB43749.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to produce mathematical evidence that confirms that reactions involving gases conform to the law of conservation of mass.

376C9FDC768045D291A5E4B51104C0AE.description: Use the ideal gas law to support the prediction of volume, mass, and number of particles produced in chemical reactions (i.e., gas stoichiometry).

9CB6F46C4ABF48D3969F47546DA568B2.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process and online simulations or lab investigations to design and model the results of controlled scientific investigations to produce mathematical evidence that confirms the gas-laws relationships.

4340CA4DBDE64E2E830E65CDE535C328.description: Use mathematical computations to describe the relationships comparing pressure, temperature, volume, and number of particles, including Boyle's law, Charles's law, Dalton's law, combined gas laws, and ideal gas laws.

6ABF180245764F45A539E12E4E8B1D0C.description: Analyze and interpret heating curve graphs to explain the energy relationship between states of matter (e.g., thermochemistry-water heating from -20oC to 120oC).

09E457C6178B43E9A0A737BFE68CD5BA.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop models (e.g., online simulations or student interactive activities) to explain and predict the behavior of each state of matter using the movement of particles and intermolecular forces to explain the behavior of matter.

C59F6CC2262446E78D3A80D8ED519F3E.description: Analyze the behavior of ideal and real gases in terms of pressure, volume, temperature, and number of particles.

D8EBCC01FEE44F05AD7831A2E801B54D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and behavior of gases.

B92DA63904AC4A09863CBE8AAC4B509E.description: Plan and conduct a controlled scientific investigation to produce mathematical evidence to predict and confirm the limiting reagent and percent yield in the reaction. Analyze quantitative data, draw conclusions, and communicate findings. Compare and analyze class data for validity.

BC2616584C0D47748C7BF2751FED6224.description: Use mathematics and computational analysis to support the concept of percent yield and limiting reagent.

3FAF3ECD7FA94401AB8E1073A592DA84.description: Plan and conduct a controlled scientific investigation to produce mathematical evidence that mass is conserved. Use percent error to analyze the accuracy of results.

2F235443FA854C25B8CD04E10A62D5C3.description: Use mathematics and computational analysis to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction. Give real-world examples (e.g., burning wood).

F5C861E6B7434F7082CE80F36B709B2D.description: Use mathematics and computational analysis to represent the ratio of reactants and products in terms of masses, molecules, and moles (stoichiometry).

B9A36C2D3E8B47F8842F7C1F05BCD058.description: Plan, conduct, and communicate the results of investigations to demonstrate different types of simple chemical reactions.

EA53A68A4B0846A88CE4EB27506AC7A4.description: Develop and use models to predict the products of chemical reactions (e.g., synthesis reactions; single replacement; double displacement; and decomposition, including exceptions such as decomposition of hydroxides, chlorates, carbonates, and acids). Discuss and/or compile lists of reactions used in everyday life.

B3288EE3B31448F29382DFB7BBE378A0.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the types, causes, and effects of chemical reactions.

4AF517C3C8824702AF0BD6CB2DE510D3.description: Generate names of ionic and covalent compounds from their formulas. Name binary compounds, binary acids, stock compounds, ternary compounds, and ternary acids.

80FE597E9E3041D08800AA7AADA312E8.description: Generate formulas of ionic and covalent compounds from compound names. Discuss compounds in everyday life and compile lists and uses of these chemicals.

14830EC995134FBFB546380FBDDB6954.description: Use the periodic table and a list of common polyatomic ions as a model to derive chemical compound formulas from compound names and compound names from chemical formulas.

85CB5C432B1D4AB5B64C523F7ADA3199.description: Students will investigate and understand the accepted nomenclature used to identify the name and chemical formulas of compounds.

BCBFB8618B334D278ECE1E488C95C60D.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to produce mathematical evidence of the empirical composition of a compound.

A1E967AD88654100A08FCAC2D60B88DF.description: Use scientific investigation to determine the percentage of composition for a substance (e.g., sugar in gum, water and/or unpopped kernels in popcorn, percent water in a hydrate). Compare results to justify conclusions based on experimental evidence.

DF0157A30A614BB99C9C8F476FD3B2BF.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to determine the empirical formula and the percent composition of compounds.

B5E1D0FB145C4A03B71754581353D5D7.description: Use models of simple hydrocarbons to exemplify structural isomerism.

3DC91383ADF64CB3A3FFDD793FD1CD34.description: Use models and oxidation numbers to predict the type of bond, shape of the compound, and the polarity of the compound.

D748AF04AC9045A398A6878E9B71AAAC.description: Predict the ionic or covalent nature of different atoms based on electronegativity trends and/or position on the periodic table.

E48C5354ED8E404DB956DF6D65D52DDE.description: Use models such as Lewis structures and ball and stick models to depict the valence electrons and their role in the formation of ionic and covalent bonds.

EA444DF4A1E44DF5822E445111E1BE13.description: Develop and use models (e.g., Lewis dot, 3-D ball-stick, 3-D printing, or simulation programs such as PhET) to predict the type of bonding between atoms and the shape of simple compounds.

2B6239BF8F194B3F90734127069774D4.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the types of bonds and resulting atomic structures for the classification of chemical compounds.

5BC60A8D3EEB48D3AB63C48DDA0F937E.description: Analyze the periodic table to identify quantum numbers (e.g., valence shell electrons, energy level, orbitals, sublevels, and oxidation numbers).

F0267437768B44CD8FB9DC0474E6A842.description: Analyze properties of atoms and ions (e.g., metal/nonmetal/metalloid behavior, electrical/heat conductivity, electronegativity and electron affinity, ionization energy, and atomic/ionic radii) using periodic trends of elements based on the periodic table.

90F79209F1D347118880732C3778210C.description: Explore and communicate the organization of the periodic table, including history, groups, families, family names, metals, nonmetals, metalloids, and transition metals.

FA0E23153B5B421DB67D71B00E8C1D15.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the periodic table as a systematic representation to predict properties of elements.

25DD693B58DA47439E91E5EB1ABBBD40.description: Research appropriate sources to evaluate the way absorption and emission spectra are used to study astronomy and the formation of the universe.

7215E62D71324D609C2EFF8E351B8631.description: Investigate absorption and emission spectra to interpret explanations of electrons at discrete energy levels using tools such as online simulations, spectrometers, prisms, flame tests, and discharge tubes. Explore both laboratory experiments and real-world examples.

5179265B080546368792825B5C5B4390.description: Construct models (e.g., ball and stick, online simulations, mathematical computations) of atomic nuclei to explain the abundance weighted average (relative mass) of elements and isotopes on the published mass of elements.

8055C36785D649808EE71C4DFAFF8780.description: Investigate the historical progression leading to the modern atomic theory, including, but not limited to, work done by Dalton, Rutherford's gold foil experiment, Thomson's cathode ray experiment, Millikan's oil drop experiment, and Bohr's interpretation of bright line spectra.

D2881492A2CA4B399A21EF985E76F9A3.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the atomic structure and the historical developments leading to modern atomic theory.

7E8536C187EA432B96874D328584F136.description: Enrichment: Research information from multiple appropriate sources and assess the credibility, accuracy, possible bias, and conclusions of each publication.

B3E77DA2F22040D4BBA4A65091DD55E4.description: Design and conduct experiments using appropriate measurements, significant figures, graphical analysis to analyze data.

954EC9DBD67E4D5783F08E897669C760.description: Use dimensional analysis (factor/label) and significant figures to convert units and solve problems.

3E2BF69AD54D49348E4491B29B397CFB.description: Students will use mathematical and computational analysis to evaluate problems.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

582D2D5729834A82ACABE336097A9397.description: Enrichment: Develop and use models to identify the functional groups that form the basis of alcohols, ketones, ethers, amines, esters, aldehydes, and organic acids.

79266DC04C8D42C987E03DD03DB6DE9F.description: Enrichment: Obtain information to communicate the system used for naming the basic linear hydrocarbons and isomers that contain single bonds, simple hydrocarbons with double and triple bonds, and simple molecules that contain a benzene ring.

6A71A485D78B470788172403A14CC3C0.description: Enrichment: Construct explanations to explain the bonding characteristics of carbon that result in the formation of basic organic molecules.

D541F37A46794A859032AD7ED95D6F4F.description: Enrichment: Students will understand that the bonding characteristics of carbon allow the formation of many different organic molecules with various sizes, shapes, and chemical properties.

AE4BFFB93CE542258DCD781CFF959FFE.description: Enrichment: Use mathematical and computational thinking to calculate an equilibrium constant expression for a reaction.

85BA70232F194401898D698E52B0B8A6.description: Enrichment: Predict when equilibrium is established in a chemical reaction.

424A871FB5264D08A03651B20664E4B0.description: Enrichment: Construct explanations to explain how to use Le Chatelier's principle to predict the effect of changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure.

5327D5D0BA2343CC8C97B1C788CAA7D8.description: Enrichment: Students will understand that chemical equilibrium is a dynamic process at the molecular level.

0D97A7B8CBC34B079A6AE3FEA5FB04DC.description: Enrichment: Use mathematical and computational thinking to solve problems involving heat flow and temperature changes, using known values of specific heat and latent heat of phase change.

22E1FBA3134C491F9FC20B1A5F8D25C2.description: Enrichment: Analyze and interpret data from energy diagrams and investigations to support claims that the amount of energy released or absorbed during a chemical reaction depends on changes in total bond energy.

DFE73CC02CAB4833AECF7DD58B45AB97.description: Enrichment: Classify chemical reactions and phase changes as exothermic or endothermic based on enthalpy values. Use a graphical representation to illustrate the energy changes involved.

C1070DEF7C124F0AAA9CE9AD2707A559.description: Enrichment: Construct explanations to explain how temperature and heat flow in terms of the motion of molecules (or atoms).

E6AD96F5EFE243069031CF6F0F57DE95.description: Enrichment: Students will understand that energy is exchanged or transformed in all chemical reactions.

A2FC12E4C4204383A3C2B684977C72CE.description: Enrichment: Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information about how buffers stabilize pH in acid-base reactions.

BFC0C3C5DDF5469B913C538CABB975C3.description: Enrichment: Use mathematical and computational thinking to calculate pH from the hydrogen-ion concentration.

8500586B44E749BBB69501CDD2F26124.description: Enrichment: Analyze and evaluate the Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry, and Lewis acid-base definitions.

F91E9B14D77F40D5968146E559C49BAF.description: Enrichment: Plan and conduct investigations using the pH scale to classify acid and base solutions.

5FF63304114C4DFF9C6432F07B86F5A9.description: Enrichment: Analyze and interpret data to identify differences between strong and weak acids and bases (i.e., dissociation).

0444C6BE992A4F0AB04EA12A5B4961F9.description: Enrichment: Analyze and interpret data to describe the properties of acids, bases, and salts.

9F1EE2883C994957AD7F091CBDCB2178.description: Enrichment: Students will understand the nature and properties of acids, bases, and salt solutions.

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

6B017000F30844078A1D8952E7371E5B.description: Enrichment: Research and communicate regarding geoscience career options (e.g., geologist, petroleum engineer, meteorologist, paleontologist, astronomer, and oceanographer.

173B9729B06B411A9CCCF56781C3EAFD.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to research, develop, and test models to aid in the responsible management of natural resources (e.g., recycling, composting, and energy usage).

2DEA3D623DD64B2B8B8A0D8A7131D6C6.description: Analyze earthquake and volcanic data to determine patterns that can lead to predicting such hazards and mitigating impact to humans.

54EB967C3E0547CB836D4D3EF5E03C8A.description: Research, assess, and communicate how Earth's systems influence the distribution of life, including how various natural hazards and geologic events (e.g., volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, landslides, tornadoes, and hurricanes) have shaped the course of human history.

BAEBA7A9DA214B2BACD6AF0CC3344926.description: Research, evaluate, and communicate about how human life on Earth shapes Earth's systems and responds to the interaction of Earth's systems (e.g., geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere). Examine how geochemical and ecological processes interact through time to cycle matter and energy and how human activity alters the rates of these processes.

6F88D75504FD458E8F49CF4E5B9B10B2.description: Students will develop an understanding of Earth's resources and the impact of human activities.

9243849D49B4484488F0731C1D9BA37E.description: Analyze and interpret the record of shared ancestry, evolution, and extinction as related to natural selection using fossils.

D8DEE813778E41BCAA6AD73B9AAED806.description: Cite evidence and develop logical arguments to identify the cause and effect relationships of the evolutionary milestones (e.g., photosynthesis and the atmosphere, the evolution of multicellular animals, the development of shells, and the colonization of terrestrial environments by plants and animals) that most profoundly shaped Earth's systems.

A3E17CB0181F41DF91EF3AFDB65AF121.description: Construct an explanation from data sets to obtain and evaluate scientific information to construct scientific arguments on changes in climate caused by various natural factors (e.g., plate tectonics and continent location and Milankovitch cycles) versus anthropogenic factors (e.g., fossil fuel use and agricultural factors).

5B7471244B514EB581DD56BD86A01D2E.description: Analyze and interpret weather data using maps and global weather systems to explain and communicate the relationships among air masses, pressure systems, and frontal boundaries.

E401F7EA719A4E8C8DC17CECFCC33961.description: Research and communicate information to explain the importance of the transfer of thermal energy among the hydrosphere, geosphere, and atmosphere. Include the unique physical and chemical properties of water, the water cycle, and energy transfer within the rock cycle.

E624981669504D85A15B89BEB2326B50.description: Explain how temperature and density of ocean water influence circulation.

05F65C9A38D74A018A73EE4B2E0D55D5.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to explore the concepts of passive solar architecture to design a structure that best utilizes solar incidence.

BCC751C7F3114721BA1D79FCF0F27473.description: Use mathematical representations (e.g., latitude, longitude, and maps) to calculate the angle of noon solar incidence and relate the value to day length, distribution of sunlight, and seasonal change.

487EDBECCF3749D78286D5DC77A351C8.description: Students will develop an understanding of Earth's systems and cycles.

ACEDD93BF17243369607369C81F160B6.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design a model to simulate the formation of caves and karst topography by groundwater.

6763AE6C336C4A419DA124A2641FCB73.description: Plan and conduct a scientific investigation to determine how factors (e.g., wind velocity, water velocity, ice, and temperature) may affect the rate of weathering.

96527955CD1A41709278B19DC9D1A36B.description: Use mathematical representations to interpret seismic graphs to triangulate the location of an earthquake's epicenter and magnitude and to correlate the frequency and magnitude of an earthquake.

CBFBB4CF94E240C29FB8E7E7C0E6F8EF.description: Research, analyze, and explain the origin of geologic features and processes that result from plate tectonics, including sea floor spreading, earthquake activity, volcanic activity, mountain building, and location of natural resources.

A9FF46EDD1834175B4E71ABA6CCFDC09.description: Use mathematical concepts to calculate the absolute age of earth materials using actual or simulated isotope ratios.

491628C2EE95488482256C3014415B36.description: Apply different techniques (e.g., superposition, original horizontality, cross-cutting relationships, lateral continuity, principle of inclusions, fossil succession, and unconformities) to analyze and interpret the relative age of actual sequences, models, or photographs.

7D24B4B8B279464588680BFB1E839843.description: Research, analyze, and evaluate the contributions of William Smith, James Hutton, Nicolaus Steno, Charles Lyell, and others to physical geology.

4DF280627518494AA03ABFA18389E2CB.description: Students will develop an understanding of the history and evolution of the earth.

5C336C632C8B469882F678C38BD30A27.description: Investigate the physical and/or chemical characteristics of rock specimens to identify and categorize igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. Include the processes that generate the transformation of rocks.

B8776ACCA1444171A576369A5E84F145.description: Investigate the physical and/or chemical characteristics of mineral specimens to identify minerals and mineral deposits/groups (e.g., oxides, carbonates, halides, sulfides, sulfates, silicates, and phosphates). Include the relationship between chemical bonds, chemical formulas, mineral use, and mineral properties.

027E0936899042B3B49B65E18E36F964.description: Analyze and interpret data to explain and communicate the differentiation of Earth's physical divisions (e.g., lithosphere and asthenosphere) using data from seismic waves and Earth's magnetic field.

B1EB39DDA4004191A7DA13F1BF5F430B.description: Analyze and interpret data to explain and communicate the differentiation of Earth's internal chemical structure (e.g., core, mantle, and crust) using the production of internal heat from the radioactive decay of unstable isotopes and gravitational energy.

BD4CDBB7DBAB4BDA89517AD0305F858D.description: Students will develop an understanding of the structure and composition of Earth and its materials.

824E6D4CAB4842C3B38DC3F44112A1D2.description: Design a model (e.g., a gravity simulation using PVC and a neoprene screen) to demonstrate Kepler's laws and the relationships of the orbits of objects in our solar system. Relate them to Newton's law of universal gravitation and laws of motion.

DD67FAC2B0984813BB4950FAD7EE7F95.description: Compare and contrast celestial bodies (e.g., planets, natural satellites, comets, asteroids, and the Oort cloud) and their motion in our solar system (e.g., revolution and rotation). Build an Analemma calendar.

3A42A68137E9428D9D550DFD435CDA73.description: Read and evaluate scientific information for mechanisms/results (e.g., the solar nebular theory) to explain how the solar system was formed. Cite evidence and develop a logical argument.

6AB55CFC691F407E9C5BD9E170760700.description: Students will develop an understanding of Earth, the solar system, and the laws that predict the motion of celestial bodies.

B8394C45DB0D48FBAD43C012EE95D2F1.description: Research and explain how nuclear fusion in stars and supernova lead to the formation of all other elements.

A3AECCFBF11441A48831314DE91536E3.description: Organize and interpret data sets for patterns and trends to compare and contrast stellar evolution in order to explain and communicate how a star changes during its life.

E5CF204D05B34538A1A63FA99B7FF5F3.description: Interpret information from the Hertzsprung -Russell diagram to differentiate types of stars, including our sun, according to size, magnitude, and classification.

7D9240139A52448A9FD90DFEF793EB9E.description: Describe the Big Bang theory and summarize observations (e.g., cosmic microwave background radiation, Hubble's law, and redshift caused by the Doppler effect) as evidence to support the formation and expansion of the universe.

02CE8911858B44D1BE93F3541368A29C.description: Students will develop an understanding of the universe, its development, immense size, and composition.

CA532047D5724D7E8F74BDECCDD83720.description: High School - Earth and Space Science

document.title: Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Science

68EAD0D624614F73AC3788CD7DCC7BAE.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to define a problem, design, construct, evaluate, and improve a device or method to reduce or prevent human impact on a natural resource (e.g., build a water filter, design an air purifier, develop a method to prevent parking lot pollution from entering a watershed).

727F10353A3F4B38AA24382D755E086E.description: Enrichment: Explore online resources related to air pollution to determine air quality in a geographic area and communicate the possible effects on the environment and human health.

35F2EAD97CFC4366A621B0261E182945.description: Enrichment: Research and analyze case studies to determine the impact of human-related and natural environmental changes on human health and communicate possible solutions to reduce/resolve the dilemma.

2C22431729944D5FA7B36C469016B5B0.description: Evaluate data and other information to explain how key natural resources (e.g., water sources, fertile soils, concentrations of minerals, and fossil fuels), natural hazards, and climate changes influence human activity (e.g., mass migrations, human health).

3BA18561A6C74D61B49B455C813E700B.description: Identify human impact and develop a solution for protection of the atmosphere, considering pollutants (e.g., acid rain, air pollution, smog, ozone layer, or increased levels of greenhouse gases) and the impacts of pollutants on human health (e.g., asthma, COPD, emphysema, and cancer).

9681F13659AF43BE9607F328BE05CD26.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interdependence of human sustainability and the environment.

3C46CE768C8642699F4009E6113EE7CA.description: Enrichment: Determine mathematically an individual's impact on the environment (carbon footprint, water usage, landfill contribution) and develop a plan to reduce personal contribution.

D5CB6CA67B8D41BBA45EFDF7289DD7C2.description: Use satellite imagery and other resources to analyze changes in biomes over time (e.g., glacial retreat, deforestation, desertification) and propose strategies to reduce the impact of human activities leading to these issues.

F8086CDA43924ADBB642CFBD67BC7F36.description: Interpret data and climate models to predict how global and regional climate change can affect Earth's systems (e.g., precipitation, temperature, impacts on sea level, global ice volumes, and atmosphere and ocean composition).

07692A4DFE9D4DFC86F2AD77719268FB.description: Use a model to describe cycling of carbon through the ocean, atmosphere, soil, and biosphere and how increases in carbon dioxide concentrations have resulted in atmospheric and climate changes.

24AC435BEF3543BABDE6984BFB7EC448.description: Students will discuss the direct and indirect impacts of certain types of human activities on the Earth's climate.

2C0BDC6978C941E9A4D8873C4689619C.description: Enrichment: Obtain water from a local source (e.g., stream on campus, rainwater, ditch water) to monitor water quality over time, using a spreadsheet program to graphically represent collected data.

3CD008FB28C3467EAF60C79BA72D2E58.description: Research various resources related to water quality and pollution (e.g., nonfictional text, EPA's Surf Your Watershed, MDEQ publications) and communicate the possible effects on the environment and human health.

241792CFE72D4490AB89080F4F5FC543.description: Examine solutions for developing, conserving, managing, recycling, and reusing energy and mineral resources to minimize impacts in natural systems (e.g., agricultural soil use, mining for coal, construction sites, and exploration of petroleum and natural gas sources).

F516A8EB32264399BFCFF05E40FD5C08.description: Compare and contrast biodegradable and nonbiodegradable wastes and their significance in landfills.

9ECC7EACE51A4798816A300A0B1BD3B4.description: Investigate and research the pros and cons of using traditional sources of energy (e.g., fossil fuels) and alternative sources of energy (e.g., water, wind, geothermal, biomass/biofuels, solar).

022AF6E4E519430CAE832121D44D4F5E.description: Differentiate between renewable and nonrenewable resources, and compare and contrast the pros and cons of using these resources.

AAED48008CCA460B83417C78E6979298.description: Students will relate the impact of human activities on the environment, conservation activities, and efforts to maintain and restore ecosystems.

7EE7429ED6B54E05975E0955A264C335.description: Enrichment: Engage in scientific argument from evidence the benefits versus harm of genetically modified organisms.

63F8311DCFA54635A31C6282A962B436.description: Evaluate and communicate data that explains how human activity may impact biodiversity (e.g., introduction, removal, and reintroduction of an organism within an ecosystem; land usage) and genetic variations of organisms, including endangered and threatened species.

409A638634D043B48404323CE4C1303B.description: Utilize data to communicate changes within a given population and the environmental factors that may have impacted these changes (e.g., weather patterns, natural disasters)

CA655BC295A24F7CA93462724E9C4D66.description: Analyze and interpret quantitative data to construct explanations of how the carrying capacity of an ecosystem may change as the availability of resources changes.

61145B1C897547F0BDD53E2AB9B8682E.description: Use mathematics, graphics, and informational text to determine how population density-dependent and density-independent limiting factors affect populations and diversity within ecosystems. Use technology to illustrate and compare a variety of population-growth curves.

665AD5365304458F915365E7772F4D68.description: Develop and use models to diagram the flow of nitrogen, carbon, and phosphorus through the environment.

968B4EDA10114BFA8F6B6F55EED3989F.description: Describe symbiotic relationships (e.g., mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism) and other co-evolutionary (e.g., predator-prey, cooperation, competition, and mimicry) relationships within specific environments.

476B7ABDAF784397BDA19F456B06158F.description: Use models to explain why the flow of energy through an ecosystem can be illustrated by a pyramid with less energy available at the higher trophic levels compared to lower levels.

98285AB6515E450385DC06E12612DC4A.description: Evaluate evidence in nonfiction text to explain how biological or physical changes within biomes affect populations and communities and how changing conditions may result in altered ecosystems.

723C390F126A4758899438EB98285CE8.description: Identify, investigate, and evaluate the interactions of the abiotic and biotic factors that determine the types of organisms that live in major biomes.

673B719C498340B4A05A45169BE642BC.description: Students will investigate the interdependence of diverse living organisms and their interactions with the components of the biosphere.

1D8F85DE0C8A45CA90E50B84596AFB78.description: Select and explain why a hypothesis, prediction, or conclusion is, or is not, supported by two or more data presentations or theoretical models.

B418321BEB004B48A1C352084408F150.description: Use new information to make a prediction based on a theoretical model.

BC52AACA46994180A4DB24301E286BDF.description: Analyze and interpret data from informational texts and data to (1) reveal patterns and construct meaning (2) support or refute hypotheses, explanations, claims or designs, or (3) evaluate the strength of conclusions.

B11291816CF94B99A51E3733BCBD46DD.description: Determine whether given information supports or contradicts a hypothesis or conclusion, and provide support for the reasoning.

58A8DF9161E645BB866DCD1C354B7463.description: Select the hypothesis, prediction, or conclusion that is, or is not, supported by data presentation or pieces of informational text.

7154B953D55B4EA8BBE7E23D7926090D.description: Students will apply scientific literacy and thinking skills to evaluate theoretical models, inferences, and experimental results found in various experimental designs including, but not limited to, those found in sample ACT science passages.

EEAA16AFFEEC48B8B9B4E864F8C065DA.description: Determine which additional trials could be performed in an investigation to enhance the results of an experimental design.

FB5870A3520C44C8AB157CAAECC847B6.description: Predict how modifying the experimental design or adding another measurement in an experimental design will affect results of the experiment.

3BF8872A158940D0B287A39B28E64A3D.description: Select and describe an alternate method for testing a hypothesis.

D59E1E342CB34B60B16ED21FDB6CD04B.description: Determine the validity of scientific questions (e.g., hypothesis) and variables for complex experimental designs.

6272840C90384BF992195EE92E793AA2.description: Analyze the methods and choice of tools used in simple and complex experimental designs.

F34FF480D97E4CBC988945D8BB389E32.description: Students will apply scientific literacy and thinking skills to analyze scientific investigations found in various experimental designs including, but not limited to, those found in sample ACT science passages.

8E88243E7B934E568E994BB923E7206C.description: Analyze presented information when given new information (e.g., given a new scenario, how would a given scenario be changed).

53B08AE054D7421AB3EFC4D0E8676EDC.description: Perform a simple interpolation or simple extrapolation using data in a table or graph. Determine and/or use a simple (e.g., linear) mathematical relationship that exists between data.

DFB3EEA96C83480293617D03600AB460.description: Translate information into a table, graph, or diagram. Determine patterns, trends, and relationships as the values of variables change.

CEE7DF6206124B2D84597C7490562413.description: Compare or combine data from two or more simple data presentations (e.g., order or sum data from a table, categorize data from a table using a scale from another table, relationships between data sets).

7784C99BF605454385A02C66444ADC3B.description: Analyze select data from a simple and complex data presentation (e.g., charts, graphs, diagrams).

7167D1656B5E448D8FEAFCFA93FD9CA5.description: Students will apply scientific literacy and thinking skills to analyze and interpret data found in various graphics including, but not limited to, those found in sample ACT science passages.

FCBB33F537354F06ACBA085428018884.description: Analyze data sets from experiments for patterns and trends and identify any weaknesses in the experimental designs.

758BC8B5227B43E5B4AEF8836EC3FBC3.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) use and manipulate appropriate metric units, (2) express relationships between variables for investigations, and (3) compare or combine data from two or more simple data presentations (e.g., order or sum data from a table, categorize data from a table using a scale from another table).

7724819B2A264BDABA6EE5AC02BE0775.description: Demonstrate the proper use of safety procedures and scientific laboratory equipment. Select and use appropriate tools and instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data.

B30D2A64EE904303B2DAA0BE054DFCD8.description: Analyze data from simple experiments and construct organized models (e.g., data tables, graphs) detailing results from the experiments.

B62AE4E72C6844BDA9E44BCE09809E2D.description: Ask questions and conduct research to generate a hypothesis, determine independent/dependent variables, and appropriate controls for scientific investigations and experiments.

BF6FDB1312A94BA783E8BD6A69FF8E17.description: Students will apply science and engineering practices and skills to scientific investigations.

EE03F969795B457ABA6DAF5C480E4860.description: Enrichment: Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions on a complex, real-world problem with numerous criteria and constraints on interactions within and between systems relevant to the problem.

D335ED2E42764BDF93A48AFB7A694C8B.description: Use an engineering design process to identify a problem within the local community, and propose and develop a possible solution for that problem.

FA98B6BFA244474BA4156DA31D951138.description: Research and present a technology that was developed through engineering design. Identify its purpose, how it has advanced through alterations in design (e.g., systems that provide homes and businesses with utilities, parking structures, park and recreational structures, and traffic flow), and careers related to its use).

8B3F6F27CBD74C6CA75FED8271B73163.description: Students will identify, research, and communicate the development of technology and engineering practices.

CE9C251E51D4440597465047102F1143.description: Enrichment: Research, analyze, explain, and communicate the influence of society, including cultural components, on the direction and progress of science and technology (e.g., medical treatments, antibiotic resistance, alternative energy development, and biomimicry).

E7E5A8CE8B654D879AAA3D7595AC93D4.description: Identify and communicate the impact of mathematics and technology in the development of scientific thought and the practice of science (e.g., space exploration, the human genome project, and ocean exploration).

39C660999D3D43A3B0FD2EF3FD543FEE.description: Research, analyze, explain, and communicate how scientific enterprise relates to society and classic inventions (e.g., microscope, telescope, computer, and telephone).

BE0B1C30ACFD41D681C3C507A36E396C.description: Trace and model the historical development of scientific ideas and theories (e.g., atomic theory, plate tectonics, evolution, genetics, discovery of cells) through the development of a timeline.

3A6317E9BE544A2EA0E7899BE3A099C7.description: Students will relate the importance of significant historical experiments and their impact on research and development.

390F4CC4C65E4195B54A2DA65C44F85F.description: History of Science and Impacts on Society

A6205C40A3104B63BB13365A0543077B.description: Enrichment: Use genomic databases for sequence analysis and apply the information to species comparisons, evolutionary relationships, and/or determine the molecular basis of inherited disorders.

F268584734084A96AB0B598B49AEB890.description: Enrichment: Apply the concept of natural selection to analyze differences in human populations (e.g., skin color, lactose persistence, sickle cell anemia, and malaria).

D4857831F6424389A098676B2A7D1087.description: Enrichment: Analyze computer simulations of the effects of natural selection on allelic frequencies in a population.

7BFFAAAB326841A9B8FA2F1A826F2E1F.description: Apply the Hardy-Weinberg formula to analyze changes in allelic frequencies due to natural selection in a population. Relate these changes to the environmental fitness of the phenotypes.

BC28EE8C54FC46BC8B2135834D32AC30.description: Describe processes that cause changes in allelic frequencies (e.g., nonrandom mating, small population size, immigration and emigration, genetic drift, and mutation).

F4E5668C95B7452F9ED8D6C561CB5683.description: Explain how natural selection acts upon genetic variability within a population and may lead to changes in allelic frequencies over time and evolutionary changes in populations.

0B25252A434B40BEAD771561CC73B272.description: Model the inheritance of chromosomes through meiotic cell division and demonstrate how meiosis and sexual reproduction lead to genetic variation in populations.

3013DAABAE6F4EC79D58D8C7AC427CE2.description: Students will apply population genetic concepts to explain variability of organisms within a population.

6B62F8427E21470CB2ACA2BC4DF6E984.description: Enrichment: Construct maps of genes on a chromosome based on data obtained from 2- and/or 3- point crosses or from recombination frequencies.

D3408FA9D8AA422796E2DA9CF4299886.description: Construct pedigrees from observed phenotypes. Analyze and interpret data to determine patterns of inheritance and disease risk.

64A2DC723215445FA0D07F730F6730B6.description: Investigate traits that follow non-Mendelian inheritance patterns (e.g., incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, autosomal linkage, sex-linkage, polygenic, and epistasis).

005A2C2DDAAC4A999731EE25F5EE8E4B.description: Illustrate Mendel's law of independent assortment by analyzing multi-trait cross data sets for patterns and trends.

196C8270E0B14788B849F756C87C6CEF.description: Demonstrate Mendel's law of dominance and segregation using mathematics to predict phenotypic and genotypic ratios.

BA5A433A4248450EBBB5A00E0B3E5433.description: Students will analyze and interpret data collected from probability calculations to explain the inheritance of traits within a population.

4D4D4AAA41DD48C88DA39FF24BB88C7B.description: Enrichment: Develop logical arguments based on scientific evidence for and against ethical concerns regarding biotechnology/bioengineering.

D0CDD51A114B497FA4AAD5773E6DF7B4.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to refine methodology and optimize the process of genetic transformation, protein purification, and/or gel electrophoresis.

2A1F3AEB22A84E41A0524387F1C5421F.description: Experimentally demonstrate genetic transformation, protein purification, and/or gel electrophoresis.

78C8807739474CE199F3BC62B0AA1DAE.description: Explain and demonstrate the use of various tools and techniques of DNA manipulation and their applications in forensics (e.g., paternity and victim/suspect identification), agriculture (e.g., pesticide or herbicide resistance, improved yields, and improved nutritional value), and personalized medicine (e.g., targeted therapies, cancer treatment, production of insulin and human growth hormone, and engineering insect vectors of human parasites).

237CCEC8B7BE4B4BAD36DEF3735A136F.description: Students will investigate biotechnology applications and bioengineering practices.

9E824E839C7A4418A52FAC2CB2D0D440.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to research the current status of genetic technology and personalized medicine, then propose and test targeted medical or forensic applications.

AA97638B46E641BF9DE969480E27E501.description: Investigate the role of mutations and the loss of cell cycle regulation in the development of cancers.

4CE3B402C2434E249750AED84C04E87D.description: Describe cellular mechanisms that can help to minimize mutations (e.g., cell cycle checkpoints, DNA polymerase proofreading, and DNA repair enzymes).

5056F1FE430F400681C57BA0690D2840.description: Explain how these mutations may result in changes in protein structure and function.

FF6E7384F2C248C8975FE324BC18F809.description: Identify factors that cause mutations (e.g., environmental, errors in replication, and viral infections).

EA8274CBB45C47558008BD0CB5E29491.description: Students will determine the causes and effects of mutations in DNA.

DB5D6F37C67444F6993107EC8112A037.description: Enrichment: Evaluate Beadle and Tatum's "One Gene-One Enzyme Hypothesis" (1941) in the development of the central dogma (DNA → RNA → Protein). Explain how new discoveries, such as alternate splicing of introns, have led to the revision of the central dogma.

0B0916E4DCB1483EB3EDB1BBAF28528E.description: Analyze the multiple roles of RNA in translation. Compare the structure and function of tRNA, rRNA, mRNA, and snRNA.

CD80D9E07DB94A38A755D1EBFDACB77D.description: Develop a model to show the relationship between the components involved in the mechanics of translation at the ribosome.

228511134A664B8CBAAB15299EC434AD.description: Describe and model how the process of transcription produces RNA from a DNA template in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

88EA4C8C396E4D17AC800F3DBCFE779D.description: Compare and contrast the structure of RNA to DNA and relate this structure to the different function of each molecule.

E240C67BDEB647E0AA40202840717A80.description: Students will analyze and explain the processes of transcription and translation in protein production.

F7519FC86EF94FBD86F5D05A5E2E5D2B.description: Microscopically observe and analyze the stages of the cell cycle (G1-S-G2-M) to describe the phenomenon, and identify methods at different cell cycle checkpoints through which the integrity of the DNA code is maintained.

B0FA03A3690447B8897AD45A8C60B106.description: Develop and use models to illustrate the mechanics of DNA replication.

8A37E3BAAB55443782A2FF4B910DBA3C.description: Compare and contrast various proposed models of DNA replication (i.e., conservative, semi-conservative, and disruptive). Evaluate the evidence used to determine the mechanism of DNA replication.

C72E1A0239D74E8DAD520684556F7B29.description: Students will analyze how the DNA sequence is copied and transmitted to new cells.

19863D2671DA468786B2C5AF1E43B65C.description: Investigate the structural differences between the genomes (i.e., circular/linear chromosomes and plasmids) found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

486AAF4B1BBE486299C8B1829B25E09C.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to refine the methodology to optimize the DNA-extraction process for various cell types.

7F6EF72E2F514007916C5202F624D3BC.description: Conduct a standard DNA extraction protocol using salt, detergent, and ethanol from various cell types (e.g., plant, animal, fungus). Compare and contrast the consistency and quantity of DNA extracted from various cell types.

C9FEAA194CF149C5B0ECB64CDB7B3BEE.description: Relate the structure of DNA to its specific functions within the cell.

5EEC503AD49B42D0BE8838431FEFF858.description: Explain the importance of the historical experiments that determined that DNA is the heritable material of the cell (Griffith, 1928; Avery, McCarty & MacLeod, 1944; Hershey & Chase, 1952).

099D6B26DE8F43EE854D9611F6E28ED2.description: Model the biochemical structure, either 3-D or computer-based, of DNA based on the experimental evidence available to Watson and Crick (Chargaff, 1950; Franklin, 1951).

301030F5387C42FAB1DE47660AD8BFC7.description: Students will demonstrate that all cells contain genetic material in the form of DNA.
