32E6817BCCCC4A66932DE7E60D5C9EEA.description: Develop and use models to illustrate the path of urine through the urinary tract.

19EE501FB0104A52BCED7862BBCFA8A0.description: Enrichment: Conduct a urinalysis to compare the composition of urine from various "patients."

F0F38BA01BCC4BE891F4A5A9CF3DF66E.description: Investigate relationship between urine composition and the maintenance of blood sugar, blood pressure, and blood volume.

9DFF7141F89345CDBC1DDE49FBFA57FD.description: Describe the processes of filtration and selective reabsorption within the nephrons as it relates to the formation of urine and excretion of excess materials in the blood.

D501FF109CBE47E3B32146A68E5DD6BE.description: Understand the structure and function of the urinary system in relation to maintenance of homeostasis.

B0DB2B223830477AA4F61C64FB971A2F.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the urinary system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

CF98462F8948466BB164BD9A12616185.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop effective treatments for gastrointestinal diseases (e.g., methods to regulate stomach acids or soothe ulcers, treat food intolerance, and dietary requirements/modifications).

9AB44D27592247F1BC2024EAE24B07F2.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., GERD/acid reflux, stomach ulcers, lactose intolerance, irritable bowel syndrome, gallstones, appendicitis, and hormonal imbalances and obesity).

4AED4B86B4BA4DEAA2993D51BDFC22FB.description: Evaluate the role of hormones (i.e., gastrin, leptin, and insulin) in the regulation of hunger and satiety/fullness.

54AF4DB9F04A4A95905E43D07C18C41F.description: Research and analyze the activity of digestive enzymes within different organs of the digestive tract, connecting enzyme function to environmental factors such as pH.

2A73957044D94C5C8F539ACD7A068541.description: Plan and conduct an experiment to illustrate the necessity of mechanical digestion for efficient chemical digestion.

AC8C099F0AE748CD9BCBE06664ADFAA8.description: Identify the accessory organs (i.e., salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas) for digestion and describe their function.

EE8AA9FBF12E41E6A83DE37ADCD00413.description: Use models to describe structural adaptations present in each organ of the tract and correlate the structures to specific processing of food at each stage (e.g., types of teeth; muscular, elastic wall and mucous lining of the stomach; villi and microvilli of the small intestine; and sphincters along the digestive tract).

A902701803274EF7AC13917DF11095CE.description: Analyze the structure-function relationship in organs of the digestive system.

059F879ABAA944D2949C8A773D36D108.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the digestive system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

882FDED99FC947378B2C0C8E9EB55250.description: Research and discuss new environmental causes of respiratory distress (e.g., e-cigarettes, environmental pollutants, and changes in inhaled gas composition).

9C360218891E4222B0166EC4080F6D9F.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., asthma, bronchitis, pneumonia, and COPD).

F1A8999DF4D840ED8DCD7A6B0B01859A.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop a model of the mechanisms that support breathing, and illustrate the inverse relationship between volume and pressure in the thoracic cavity.

E622595880EC483E82548D9B3D4AB863.description: Identify the five mechanics of gas exchange: pulmonary ventilation, external respiration, transport gases, internal respiration, and cellular respiration.

813E56ECAC6B4D2EA87549D4EB90AED8.description: Describe structural adaptations of the respiratory tract and relate these structural features to the function of preparing incoming air for gas exchange at the alveolus.

A907ED55C4224E04A23E7B227CABB6B5.description: Design and use models to illustrate the functions of the organs of the respiratory system.

EC2222AB23E34A9597505540705540F6.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the respiratory system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

1DC4B7DABF72468889082F6495790E71.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., viral infections, auto-immune disorders, immunodeficiency disorders, and lymphomas).

F8D51A78A2334E9AA14A5CA01318AC3E.description: Investigate various forms of acquired and passive immunity (e.g., fetal immunity, breastfed babies, vaccinations, and plasma donations).

461567007E314ACE810014CC316DFF21.description: Differentiate the role of B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes in the development of humoral and cell-mediated immunity and primary and secondary immune responses.

05D869312E2F4365B2CC0E2E00D8680A.description: Correlate the functions of the spleen, thymus, lymph nodes, and lymphocytes to the development of immunity.

F702F181997042199053276A4A83E2CC.description: Compare and contrast the body's non-specific and specific lines of defense, including an analysis of the roles of various leukocytes: basophils, eosinophils, neutrophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes.

FAC82578AB964E378A924439D1099E82.description: Compare the primary functions of the lymphatic system and its relationship to the cardiovascular system.

BC2D0D66A3E24675B16E20557080F9CC.description: Analyze the functions of leukocytes, lymph, and lymphatic organs in the immune system.

19F3CD7810664792867D6AAA853A103C.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the lymphatic system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

38E3CBF03DCB4C52A1A4A64EB33A7683.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop, model, and test effective treatments for cardiovascular diseases (e.g., methods to regulate heart rate, artificial replacement valves, open blood vessels, or strengthening leaky valves).

F666CDC11F6246E2A857C4B036782F14.description: Research and analyze the effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., hypertension, myocardial infarction, mitral valve prolapse, varicose veins, and arrhythmia).

770FA5A42EB941A486FBB320BA6D3C5E.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to test the effects of various stimuli on heart rate and/or blood pressure. Construct graphs to analyze data and communicate conclusions.

B954EC728C5F459BA60C98CC17D34543.description: Demonstrate the role of valves in regulating blood flow.

B378B432DDB2437F821FBF7A30D1EE7A.description: Investigate the structure and function of different types of blood vessels (e.g., arteries, capillaries, veins). Identify the role each plays in the transport and exchange of materials.

714E1A3FC5274343813FFF96D8412DFA.description: Describe the flow of blood through the pulmonary system and systemic circulation.

C3CBE20C8A5545E0B3E948215252506F.description: Design and use models to investigate the functions of the organs of the cardiovascular system.

E397E2375B63460CB1ADA0B3B981B167.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the cardiovascular system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

D1FA991D20B5484C8A952CCEE5BDA413.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop effective treatments for blood disorders (e.g., methods to regulate blood cell counts or blood doping tests).

FD22E4962C4A418B97034EFD11D0CE71.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., anemia, malaria, leukemia, hemophilia, and blood doping).

1223C45431E34267BE6059E315A04999.description: Distinguish the cellular difference between the ABO blood groups and investigate blood type differences utilizing antibodies to determine compatible donors and recipients.

7A24B9CFF66D4E398ACF09D3FEF7500C.description: Describe the structure, function, and origin of the cellular components and plasma components of blood.

A499C4CC5DA745C0A32F60B035154EE5.description: Students will analyze the structure and functions of blood and its role in maintaining homeostasis.

AB85A3BBAD8746D9B8757CEB21797F9F.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., infertility, ovarian cysts, endometriosis, sexually transmitted diseases, and ectopic pregnancy). Research current treatments for infertility.

54D5EAA354A84D34805899575DEE062F.description: Describe the changes that occur during embryonic/fetal development, birth, and the growth and development from infancy, childhood, and adolescence to adult.

02488FB17F4743C38BC9C49D5717CBF8.description: Evaluate and communicate information about various contraceptive methods to prevent fertilization and/or implantation.

DF18CED61D1E48ADB7DF8846225545EC.description: Construct explanations detailing the role of hormones in the regulation of sperm and egg development. Analyze the role of negative feedback in regulation of the female menstrual cycle and pregnancy.

ED58F0CBFA9C48BCAB69E00AAFAAC327.description: Describe the female reproductive anatomy and relate structure to egg production and release.

0DEB259FAD71491DA9FE81A464F2CA03.description: Describe the male reproductive anatomy and relate structure to sperm production and release.

16009E87126E43BAA0F70C54742A8ACB.description: Compare and contrast the structure and function of the male and female reproductive systems.

3D2F91C88F924AB2ACB0FCD9A659C477.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the male and female reproductive system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

E80C715D53A442E6A8719E2B7C8BA178.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop effective treatments for endocrine disorders (e.g., methods to regulate hormonal imbalance).

345C8512E8FE4CB5A858C23E1D232FEF.description: Research and analyze the effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus, pituitary dwarfism, Graves' disease, Cushing's syndrome, hypothyroidism, and obesity).

90B00EE9128D4540A7501D137EC502A4.description: Model specific mechanisms through which the endocrine system maintains homeostasis (e.g., insulin/glucagon and glucose regulation; T3 / T4 and metabolic rates; calcitonin/parathyroid and calcium regulation; antidiuretic hormone and water balance; growth hormone; and cortisol and stress).

3BB37B9A2AC046C7970C8C7DF91B6C40.description: Discuss the function of each endocrine gland and the various hormones secreted.

94FE5EDA22EE41298EF4BBF999B6EB47.description: Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to illustrate that the endocrine glands secrete hormones that help the body maintain homeostasis through feedback mechanisms.

5404655496D64896B50FFB5783D70C77.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the major organs of the endocrine system and the associated hormonal production and regulation.

B4FED698E8074D73845107253E236D40.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop, model, and test preventative devices for neurological injuries and/or disorders (e.g., concussion-proof helmets or possible medications for addiction and depression).

67041EE8CD334D0BBAEDC6A7F77F92B6.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., addiction, depression, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's, sports-related chronic traumatic encephalopathy [CTE], dementia, chronic migraine, stroke, and epilepsy).

10CECECC299C4810AC6453133AFE81EE.description: Describe the structure and function of the special senses (i.e., vision, hearing, taste, and olfaction).

8C2D0818A3E64CFEB0DDCA9459C6F22C.description: Describe the major characteristics of the autonomic nervous system. Contrast the roles of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems in maintaining homeostasis.

20A4A9E812884DF081A7E7E732E489D1.description: Enrichment: Plan and conduct an experiment to test reflex response rates under varying conditions. Using technology, construct graphs in order to analyze and interpret data to explain and communicate conclusions.

682892870C8643C783E461FF36236168.description: Compare and contrast the structures and functions of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Investigate how the systems interact to maintain homeostasis (e.g., reflex responses, sensory responses).

AD8A824A5EA047C9A6862B393623E71B.description: Discuss the structure and function of the brain and spinal cord.

ADCFCC9C6FEC4989800DFA83E3BF6354.description: Analyze the structure and function of neurons and their supporting neuroglia cells (e.g. astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, Schwann cells, microglial).

16CA2635B21B4315A8B4975641ADD86E.description: Describe and evaluate how the nervous system functions and interconnects with all other body systems.

580FE1FA01C54F518FC28039D24D1BB2.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the nervous system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

D8BD29E161D14A93ADDA1DBB1F2FBB49.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop effective ergonomic devices to prevent muscle fatigue and strain (e.g., carpal tunnel, exoskeletons for paralysis, or training plans to prevent strains/sprains/cramps).

003257DD5E924867808D65BF4B9D2EC6.description: Use technology to plan and conduct an investigation that demonstrates the physiology of muscle contraction, muscle fatigue, or muscle tone. Collect and analyze data to interpret results, then explain and communicate conclusions.

813856722B414A33B83DD70B5C8E174C.description: Compare and contrast the anatomy and physiology of the three types of muscle tissue.

07CF57501CE3479DBE5FE411E5FE00D7.description: Use models to locate the major muscles and investigate the movements controlled by each muscle.

2089875D2D5F4D3E97210C66CBC0D98E.description: Explain the molecular mechanism of muscle contraction and relaxation.

17A619BD685C4A21A231BDDFD2DB2218.description: Describe the structure and function of the skeletal muscle fiber and the motor unit.

A4829B9ECE0D46798A73016187941AEB.description: Develop and use models to illustrate muscle structure, muscle locations and groups, actions, origins, and insertions.

4887B84EA5CA42CBB65B721D0BE35B14.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the muscular system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

807DF5452C224813A5893A5A786436E0.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to develop, model, and test effective treatments for bone disorders (i.e., prosthetics).

9529C7E193A547729B018F3EFE702414.description: Research and analyze various pathological conditions (e.g., bone fractures, osteoporosis, bone cancers, various types of arthritis, and carpal tunnel syndrome).

418329BCFBD745158970A410B2D18B6B.description: Construct explanations detailing how mechanisms (e.g., Ca²+ regulation) are used by the skeletal system to maintain homeostasis.

166ACED90BDD403D966E5AF0C26512DC.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the growth and development of the skeletal system, differentiating between endochondral and intramembranous ossification.

AD96CEF9D24D4995A235506E45F7C62B.description: Identify and classify types of joints and their movement.

2DD4A77F89C54F698AB07ED738EE4B10.description: Develop and use models to identify and classify major bones as part of the appendicular or axial skeleton.

53B83024F25A49FFAB2AF5E2A213A24A.description: Use models to compare the structure and function of the skeletal system.

4866FF12A3984DBEBA57440E066C0CE1.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the skeletal system including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

E66BE2A07FCF4DB89D0A2ABAAA602755.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design and model/simulate effective treatments for skin disorders (e.g., tissue grafts).

6989F33468AC4ED59DE1EB71356DDA52.description: Research and analyze the causes and effects of various pathological conditions (e.g., burns, skin cancer, bacterial/viral infections, and chemical dermatitis).

58C03A87A1454930813B871E52FBDDD5.description: Investigate specific mechanisms (e.g., feedback and temperature regulation) through which the skin maintains homeostasis.

1A4E6403D5694E518643920EB5CBA923.description: Identify structures and explain the functions of the integumentary system, including layers of skin, accessory structures, and types of membranes.

AC1320809D834DCE84A49DD65141ACA3.description: Students will investigate the structures and functions of the integumentary system, including the cause and effect of diseases and disorders.

35893B602E70487B9231AD8946C60BB1.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to research and develop medications (i.e., targeted cancer therapy drugs) that target uncontrolled cancer cell reproduction.

92B8F5FC30D54CDEBA7F24A052EA2573.description: Construct a model to demonstrate how the structural organization of cells in a tissue relates to the specialized function of that tissue.

041558B9372E4AA887AC3D70C3DDE471.description: Analyze the characteristics of the four main tissue types: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous. Examine tissues using microscopes and other various technologies.

3D8B00088F3E41C08D491B33C041F737.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship of cells and tissues that form complex structures of the body.

BFA9B5572F3C4F7B84D4F6251B1B1766.description: Investigate the interdependence of the various body systems to each other and to the body as a whole.

9A0C7D1A7CA94FA9A40E1919E6545D99.description: Locate organs and their applicable body cavities and systems.

125355DC06EB47629669D15403164604.description: Apply appropriate anatomical terminology when explaining the orientation of regions, directions, and body planes or sections.

F93FA8B79E104E209930083AC6BB70AF.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of how anatomical structures and physiological functions are organized and described using anatomical position.

96B9DEA0D7AA4F8896B2670A164B0533.description: Enrichment: Choose an environmental issue that currently exists in one of the aquatic ecosystems and use an engineering design process to propose and develop a possible solution using scientific knowledge and best management practices (BMPs). Create an environmental action plan to include moral, legal, societal, political, and economic decisions that impact animal diversity in both the short and long term. Results from developed plans will be communicated with classmates.

893E33017269478BAAD224E3F4958901.description: Research, analyze, and communicate which and in what capacity local, state, and federal regulatory agencies are involved in different aquatic ecosystems, including current environmental policies already in place (e.g., the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act). Research should include, but is not limited to, how humans can preserve animal diversity through the use of habitat creation and conservation, research, legislation, medical and breeding programs, and management of genetic diversity at local and global levels.

6BC594D56B6043A798E1A7B08EC3C044.description: Research, analyze, and communicate the effects of natural phenomena (e.g., hurricanes, floods, drought, and sea-level rise) on the aquatic ecosystems.

41C8E363BB684947BB933553CB6F04BF.description: Explore the importance of species diversity to the biological resources needed by human populations, including food (e.g., aquaculture and mariculture), medicine, and natural aesthetics.

C4A8F75F1FBB42A7A46CA7E5AC5F6752.description: Research, analyze, and communicate the effects of urbanization and continued expansion by humans on the aquatic ecosystems' biodiversity (e.g., land use changes, erosion and sedimentation, over-fishing, invasive/exotic species, and pollution).

7F3B3B025B7A4F4E848747899CB67C73.description: Determine the niches within trophic levels in the aquatic ecosystems by creating food webs and researching the symbiotic relationships that exist.

8A7DCA33C66E420E8437529B8A532F47.description: Recognize representative examples of plants and animals that would be specifically adapted to the aquatic ecosystems, and identify adaptations necessary to survive.

754A544AA0E44C36BFB5B695EA18A17A.description: Compare and contrast the unique biotic and abiotic characteristics of the following selected aquatic ecosystems: intertidal zone, wetlands/estuaries, coral reef, barrier islands, continental slope/shelf, abyss, rivers/streams/watersheds, and lakes/ponds.

D10DE7A336D74B0BBE7B8F0E76A80044.description: Students will examine characteristics of specific aquatic ecosystems and the effects of human and natural phenomena on those ecosystems.

BDF4E8B04A6D4197963DED45816F1F8E.description: Classify zones of freshwater sources based on the velocity of current, depth, and temperature.

E6158E4898864BE29AFB5565020FEA0B.description: Classify zones of the ocean based on distance from shorelines (i.e., intertidal, neritic, oceanic, and benthic zones), temperature, and light availability (i.e., epipelagic, mesopelagic, bathypelagic, abyssopelagic, and hadopelagic).

7EA4DBD6E25A4E49A14BD004ADF62025.description: Develop an understanding of plate tectonics to predict certain geological features (e.g., sea floor spreading, paleomagnetic measurements, and orogenesis).

29A39109161F426A94F0E4925C751E8E.description: Use geospatial data to analyze, explain, and communicate differences among the major geological features of specific aquatic ecosystems (e.g., plate tectonics, continental rise, continental slope, abyssal plain, trenches, sea mounts, island formation, and watersheds).

D6A25D984D5A40CA908C9A486CD9F98A.description: Students will understand the principles of plate tectonics, sea floor spreading, and physical features of oceanic zones.

FA932639E9E14E349B29D969F8102F0A.description: Distinguish among lentic and lotic water systems, including water flow, seasonal overturn, and watershed mapping.

AD2D8FBBD0C5462E8E3F0E7FEE82E39F.description: Research, analyze, and communicate scientific arguments to support climate models that predict how global and regional climate change can affect Earth's systems (e.g., precipitation and temperature and their associated impacts on sea level, global ice volumes, and atmosphere and ocean composition).

FD5A3BD82B7C416AA7F1CC94730FEAFC.description: Summarize principles related to currents (e.g., global wind patterns, Coriolis effect, Ekman spiral, surface, thermohaline, upwelling, downwelling, El Niño, La Niña, hurricanes, Barrier Island movement).

A65C953F5FDA4796B5F022F8D306DA46.description: Survey predictable patterns of tides (i.e., tidal period and range, diurnal, semidiurnal, mixed, spring, and neap tides) to correlate with moon phases in graphical form.

428CA8EDD7C34F3E9267ACCF0FB74DD5.description: Characterize wave features and wave properties, including wavelength, period, wave speed, breakers, and constructive waves and their effects on shoreline communities (e.g., headlands, embayments, shoreline erosion, and deposition).

8AB9CA03FF694A9F8FC96FB9B1FC7BB6.description: Students will develop an understanding of the principles of fluid dynamics as it relates to both salt and freshwater systems.

24FC5DCB0EE0412D82F6019D7F193521.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to reduce the effects of pollution in aquatic ecosystems (e.g., microplastics, garbage patches, oil spills, and eutrophication). Students will design a proposed solution based on current research and/or observations, and develop a model in order to test their design. Data from experimentation will be analyzed, organized graphically, and communicated to classmates to determine the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

266E941120C34BF78558352132ECD7E3.description: Research, analyze, and communicate current technology and career opportunities available to collect this data on a global scale using CTD, buoy data, or satellites.

5362D75D5FE94DACB31B504CE1F619B1.description: Collect, analyze, and communicate quantitative data that includes dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, salinity, mineral content, nitrogen compounds, and turbidity from an aquatic environment (i.e., hydrometer, refractometer, Secchi disk, and chemical test kits).

0DFCFA72E46E4CE78C1C0FA6D0D09A7E.description: Diagram, utilizing digital or physical models, the water cycle and how it relates to the total amount of fresh water available to living things at any given time.

3CE7A58C0A6B4B2D8D9F2441ABC4467A.description: Describe the role of water within biological systems (e.g., provides the medium necessary to allow for life processes such as protein synthesis, enzymatic reactions, and passive transport).

1F4A469405EF4392870D9BB1B4878734.description: Characterize the physical and chemical properties of water, including specific heat, surface temperature, universal solvent, and hydrogen bonding between water molecules (i.e., cohesion/adhesion/capillary action).

1786102752D94CDAB68281B1A00D0CF2.description: Students will develop an understanding of the unique physical and chemical properties of water and how those properties shape life on earth.

C8A4A43E71204AFEA3FE27109429CFE3.description: Enrichment: Given a niche in a specific environment, use an engineering design process to design an animal, listing characteristics based on your knowledge of shared and derived characteristics, internal and external anatomy, and how the animal would adapt morphologically and physiologically relative to its ecological role and specific environment.

434A3E7CA2E547DA86C370EB9BC8E1FC.description: Using key morphological and physiological adaptations found within aquatic vertebrate taxa, assess how animals interact with their environment to determine their ecological roles.

B3FABA0B907B4CD6B2FAC9CD655C49E4.description: Dissect representative taxa (e.g., shark, fish); collect data; compare their internal and external anatomy; and analyze, explain, and communicate results.

510E6A9D46134C97A94F4E73F8BB4134.description: Differentiate various life cycles found among animals (e.g., egg, tadpole, and adult stages of the amphibian life cycle; leathery eggs on land in reptiles; hard-shelled eggs in Aves; placental, marsupial, or monotremes in mammals; viviparous, ovoviviparous, and oviparous animals).

5560D6B3CA8148629DEBB249CE9DA3EC.description: Utilize a dichotomous key to identify select aquatic vertebrates.

5E200FD95CE44E6EB4F7D32A69EA1800.description: Identify characteristics that are shared and derived using graphical representation of animal evolution, and develop cladograms/phylogenetic trees.

D0502DF91E4F46ED99642A500ADFC5D7.description: Characterize aquatic representatives of the following taxa: Hemichordata, Urochordata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata (including Agnatha, Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, and Mammalia).

4D73F1F09712482188C641518710CB84.description: Students will investigate characteristics of aquatic invertebrates.

F4D7C89345BA4DA9878CA119CAA7E893.description: Enrichment: Given a niche in a specific environment, use an engineering design process to design an animal, listing characteristics based on your knowledge of shared and derived characters, internal and external anatomy, and how the animal would adapt morphologically and physiologically relative to its ecological role and specific environment.

3099B664E7414090BB367FED79D897AA.description: Using key morphological and physiological adaptations found within animal taxa, assess how animals interact with their environment to determine their ecological roles.

093AAEDA4605450CADBBF1C809773604.description: Dissect representative taxa (e.g., clam and squid), collect data, compare their internal and external anatomy, analyze, explain, and communicate results.

1339BC8CF1CB43D8B0781DF0DEA07B2D.description: Explain various life cycles found among animals (e.g., polyp and medusa in cnidarians, multiple hosts and stages in the platyhelminthic life cycle, and arthropod metamorphosis).

133038E6606945258080FAFCD6F806C2.description: Compare and contrast major body plans (e.g., asymmetry, radial, bilateral symmetry, acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, and eucoelomate).

4ACD93A3CCC74083BCFB5BD6BFBE72FA.description: Develop a dichotomous classification key to be used in the identification of sample aquatic invertebrates.

80B13ECC9C3B41E78FA3A289E3637566.description: Identify characteristics that are shared and derived using graphical representations of animal evolution (i.e., cladograms and phylogenetic trees) and develop cladograms and phylogenetic trees.

5C6499FD23834A71833F52A7F4DFACB9.description: Characterize aquatic representatives of the following taxa: Protozoa (e.g., foraminiferians, radiolarians, amoeba, and paramecium), Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Rotifera, Mollusca, Arthropoda, Bryozoa, Brachiopoda, and Echinodermata.

00F6A3142B5542E69448CF19BE761CA7.description: Students will investigate characteristics of aquatic invertebrates.

FA08249EBC684BCFA5B585C4B7028B4F.description: Enrichment: Research, analyze, and communicate historical and current methodologies for measuring primary productivity. Use an engineering design process to design and develop improvements to measure primary productivity (e.g., the light and dark bottle method and satellite data).

1D15BCEA2EC04827B251DAEB1BB98DF8.description: Paraphrase energy conversion processes (e.g., photosynthesis and chemosynthesis).

323620CC82724D229CEFEC89B1D969DE.description: Use dichotomous keys to identify sample producers within an aquatic ecosystem.

54DC414DC8F7413888FD346C1FC91849.description: Recognize characteristics that are shared and derived using graphical representations of primary-producer evolution and develop cladograms/phylogenetic trees.

38AEFD6A2E54486687E5C72E8D43C591.description: List and describe common autotrophs that may be found in particular aquatic ecosystems, including prokaryotes (e.g., Cyanobacteria and Archaebacteria), protists (e.g., diatoms, dinoflagellates, green algae, kelp, sargassum, and red algae), and plants (e.g., cord grasses, reeds, seagrasses, and mangroves).

F72738DAE17E4F1EB635F7394B7A2285.description: Survey common primary producers and their roles in primary production in relation to geographical distribution within various aquatic ecosystems.

DEDB9D15B80F48C289FF5DF1E9170F2B.description: Students will explore the biodiversity and interactions among aquatic life.

59738E9020F141FDAB0F9DB4C89EC825.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to construct a working electric motor to perform a task. Communicate the design process and comparisons of task performance efficiencies.

81253A79866F41819D9F2018C55AEC54.description: Distinguish between magnets, motors, and generators, and evaluate modern industrial uses of each.

9911B2AD43984B8299116C992117C43F.description: Use digital resources and online simulations to investigate the basic principles of electricity, including static electricity, current electricity, and circuits. D34D27418F2F4E26A65E2433D683C634.description: Students will explore basic principles of magnetism and electricity (e.g., static electricity, current electricity, and circuits).

58760E80713D450EBD40545139AB0EB2.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to construct a simulation of heat energy transfer between systems. Calculate the calories/joules of energy generated by burning food products. Communicate conclusions based on evidence from the simulation.

975FFFBA47094A8A8AB4A74BB053F72B.description: Relate thermal energy transfer to real world applications of conduction (e.g., quenching metals), convection (e.g., movement of air masses/weather/plate tectonics), and radiation (e.g., electromagnetic).

B6B22BF4527841F8AA5C0980A036B04C.description: Apply particle theory to phase change and analyze freezing point, melting point, boiling point, vaporization, and condensation of different substances.

D737E9F8AFE542EFA2BB4C3F6D3E546C.description: Compare and contrast temperature scales by converting between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin.

E75F110C0EDB4DCB9A0E958701B3F937.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of temperature scales, heat, and thermal energy transfer.

13D6A7307C804103975D0425DFBF3AB2.description: Conduct investigations to provide evidence of the conservation of energy as energy is converted from one form of energy to another (e.g., wind to electric, chemical to thermal, mechanical to thermal, and potential to kinetic).

E5FEEEDB09A24AB293B155C4A9634C1F.description: Using mathematical and computational analysis, calculate potential and kinetic energy based on given data. Use equations such as PE=mgh and KE=½ mv².

2244DA255B36431C80BAA2684504D395.description: Use scientific investigations to explore the transformation of energy from one type to another (e.g., potential to kinetic energy, and mechanical, chemical, electrical, thermal, radiant, and nuclear energy interactions).

7951E6E8A75449F3A04A1D59D0696F4F.description: Using digital resources, explore forms of energy (e.g., potential and kinetic energy, mechanical, chemical, electrical, thermal, radiant, and nuclear energy).

E9DF997DEDEC4648821ACEB95936A6AC.description: Students will examine different forms of energy and energy transformations.

7437E833F4544CC194310A13D4E1D2BD.description: Enrichment: Debate the particle/wave behavior of light.

96A7209DDEFD4185959636AC3F714438.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design and construct an apparatus that forms images to project on a screen or magnify images using lenses and/or mirrors.

779BC867E43045F8B09D176944C6D252.description: Research real-world applications to create models or visible representations of the electromagnetic spectrum, including visible light, infrared radiation, and ultraviolet radiation.

18C33809CBAE462F878D0A1B4CCA71A1.description: Design and conduct experiments to investigate technological applications of sound (e.g., medical uses, music, acoustics, Doppler effects, and influences of mathematical theory on music).

767FC3B7E8E4478DAB53B855278E66D0.description: Enrichment: Use an engineering design process to design and build a musical instrument to demonstrate the influence of resonance on music.

B72B260467A14BEFB6911CC55B902707.description: Generate wave models to explore energy transference.

5D6DE50359FF4B389998DFF7C38D18E6.description: Analyze examples and evidence of transverse and longitudinal waves found in nature (e.g., earthquakes, ocean waves, and sound waves).

427EBEC82BF74A03B21C7AA92FBA5B00.description: Use models to analyze and describe examples of mechanical waves' properties (e.g., wavelength, frequency, speed, amplitude, rarefaction, and compression).

65E271D845BE41E2A762218777B1B05E.description: Students will explore the characteristics of waves.

943A50A347EF425C81828ED802153AE0.description: Research the efficiency of everyday machines, and debate ways to improve their economic impact on society (e.g., electrical appliances, transportation vehicles).

C35EBD1E444846019E284B86DA3C479D.description: Use mathematical and computational representations to create graphs and formulas that describe the relationships between force, work, and energy (i.e., W=Fd, KE=½ mv², PE=mgh, W=KE).

28B58F6131AC40CF8A69105F63033D1D.description: Use an engineering design process and mathematical analysis to design and construct models to demonstrate the law of conservation of momentum (e.g., roller coasters, bicycle helmets, bumper systems).

7218BC105E9F40FFA76D91D348261DAD.description: Design and construct an investigation using probe systems and/or online simulations to observe relationships between force, mass, and acceleration (F=ma).

C30A11767728495BB35E45A9891A827D.description: Use mathematical and computational analyses to show the relationships among force, mass, and acceleration (i.e., Newton's second law).

1982D34F5C1546E7B9C1E85D89A3AEE4.description: Collect, organize, and interpret graphical data using correct metric units to determine the average speed of an object.

0EAE28F16F1D49C187C4666FC2C8C223.description: Design and conduct an investigation to study the motion of an object using properties such as displacement, time of motion, velocity, and acceleration.

F9DAB46C093F48A4BD4E1D567D027632.description: Research the scientific contributions of Newton, and use models to communicate Newton's principles.

D4E4764CA7BB4C7A9A84DDD33C8EC7A5.description: Students will analyze the scientific principles of motion, force, and work.

AF2F78095C0C4BFD9918B3510A272249.description: Analyze and debate the advantages and disadvantages of nuclear reactions as energy sources.

FBE8C4739A324822971EB7894EE0C885.description: Research nuclear reactions and their uses in the modern world, exploring concepts such as fusion, fission, stars as reactors, nuclear energy, and chain reactions.

3FE9D68AD23940388A3D8E8BD605D175.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to examine evidence that mass is conserved in chemical reactions using simple stoichiometry problems (1:1 mole ratio) or atomic masses to demonstrate the conservation of mass with a balanced equation.

DAA99B647EE048B8BFF1216133AAACAD.description: Apply the concept of conservation of matter to balancing simple chemical equations.

278D9B4B0D584EE784AE8E7418A0F22D.description: Design and conduct investigations to produce evidence that mass is conserved in chemical reactions (e.g., vinegar and baking soda in a Ziploc© bag).

5C22B4795DD24B3C80879D3FAFA61016.description: Design and conduct experiments to investigate physical and chemical changes of various household products (e.g., rusting, sour milk, crushing, grinding, tearing, boiling, and freezing) and reactions of common chemicals that produce color changes or gases.

65F218D7C261455190FE2F2F3437405D.description: Students will analyze changes in matter and the relationship of these changes to the law of conservation of matter and energy.

DE31451D2ADF471CB7C67668709F4672.description: The Law of Conservation of Matter and Energy

3762D014A7D444CEB519026F0ADA0B18.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to determine the atomic mass of binary compounds.

88D5A6B7323E46418C35CEAFB2A92F6F.description: Use naming conventions to name common acids and common compounds used in classroom labs (e.g., sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), NaHCO3; hydrochloric acid, HCl; sulfuric acid, H2SO4 ; acetic acid (vinegar), HC2H3O2; and nitric acid, HNO3).

6FBB43F5A3324B28888EAB72DE33992E.description: Using naming conventions for binary compounds, write the compound name from the formula, and write balanced formulas from the name (e.g., carbon dioxide - CO<sub>2</sub>, sodium chloride - NaCl, iron III oxide- Fe2O3, and calcium bromide - CaBr<sub>2</sub>).

E89BA08C56C74F34B86A238C9E7ABA58.description: Using the periodic table and scientific methods, investigate the formation of compounds through ionic and covalent bonding.

42B0B798311E41F5A0B7ED5F26DA7B4E.description: Use contextual evidence to determine the organization of the periodic table, including metals, metalloids, and nonmetals; symbols; atomic number; atomic mass; chemical families/groups; and periods/series.

8DB4EAEE9746446EA449ABF8756F576A.description: Students will analyze the organization of the periodic table of elements to predict atomic interactions.

8C24F8A837304D878C44DDBDEE4A815C.description: Research and develop models (e.g., 3-D models, online simulations, or ball and stick) to investigate both modern and historical theories of atomic structure. D392B5F60D0247F3A155600BC366F13A.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of both modern and historical theories of atomic structure.

99D7AD88E4C84BF799E738F7EEAC26EA.description: Use mathematical and computational analysis to solve density problems. Manipulate the density formula to determine density, volume, or mass or use dimensional analysis to solve problems.

1CE6457C75594FE3B13CA431A7A73902.description: Design and conduct an investigation using graphical analysis (e.g., line graph) to determine the density of liquids and/or solids.

117157141E484DC483DD705F1E360B07.description: Design and conduct investigations to explore techniques in measurements of mass, volume, length, and temperature.

187C7EA7E06945F1B4A5F232283F9C30.description: Conduct an investigation to determine the identity of unknown substances by comparing properties to known substances.

F2742926952C4EC188BBA615EFD7D4EB.description: Use scientific research to generate models to compare physical and chemical properties of elements, compounds, and mixtures.

932EB41C2A8E46FB8BB325FCB2E6D584.description: Use contextual evidence to describe particle theory of matter. Examine the particle properties of solids, liquids, and gases.

3AF8811A84304F97B8B275E895EB5D2D.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the nature of matter.

58D063E3CCB145A293A37E18CCE70F3B.description: Explore the mass number and atomic number of the nucleus of an isotope of a given chemical element.

EE28B8CDF7B1468BB7379CB52DB3F5F3.description: Analyze and explain the concepts of nuclear physics.

4895928882034709BC40A662F3DFC86C.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the basic principles of nuclear energy.

P.A.T.R.I.O.T. Act, Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Homeland Security).

F5A11CD1A21548909935560241954AA4.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
